If they say: Since the occurrence of that disgrace necessarily entails the occurrence of this victory, singling it out for mention is pointless. We say: The matter is not so, for it is possible that disgrace befalls them at the hands of the believers, yet the believers suffer some calamity from another cause. So when He said, ﴿and give you victory over them,﴾ it indicated that they benefit from this victory, conquest, and triumph.

The fourth: His saying: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾ We have mentioned that the Khuza'a had embraced Islam, and Quraysh aided Banu Bakr against them until they inflicted punishment upon them. So God healed their breasts from Banu Bakr. It is well known that whoever has long suffered harm from his adversary, and then God empowers him over him in the best manner, his joy in it greatly increases, and that becomes a cause of strength of the soul and steadfastness of resolve.

The fifth: His saying: ﴿and remove the rage of their hearts.﴾

One might say: His saying, ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people,﴾ means that He heals them from the pain of rage, and this is the very same as removing rage, so His saying, ﴿and remove the rage of their hearts,﴾ is a repetition.

The answer is that He promised them the occurrence of this conquest, so they were in the crush of waiting, as it is said: "Waiting is the red death." So He healed their breasts from the crush of waiting. On this interpretation, the difference between His saying, ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people,﴾ and His saying, ﴿and remove the rage of their hearts,﴾ becomes clear.

These are the five benefits that God, exalted is He, mentioned in this fighting, and all of them return to calming the motives arising from the irascible faculty (al-quwwa al-ghadabiyya), namely the desire for vengeance, the seeking of retribution, and the removal of rage. He did not mention in them the finding of wealth or the attainment of food and drink, because the Arabs are a people created with zeal and pride, so He encouraged them in these meanings, which are suited to their natures. There remain here some points:

The first point: these attributes are suitable for the conquest of Mecca, because what took place in that event resembles these circumstances, and for this reason it is permissible to say that the verse was revealed concerning it.

The second point: the verse indicates a miracle (mu'jiza), because He, exalted is He, reported the occurrence of these circumstances, and they did occur in accordance with these reports, so this is a report of the unseen, and reports of the unseen are a miracle.

The third point: this verse indicates that the Companions were believers in the knowledge of God, exalted is He, with true faith, because it indicates that their hearts were filled with anger, with zeal for the sake of religion, and with an intense desire for the exaltation of the religion of Islam, and these states do not arise except in the hearts of believers.

Know that God's describing them with this does not negate that they are described as merciful and compassionate, for He, exalted is He, said of them: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 54], and He also said: ﴿severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

Then He said: ﴿God turns in forgiveness to whom He wills.﴾ Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: This is mentioned by way of resumption (isti'naf), and it cannot be a response to His saying, ﴿Fight them,﴾ because His saying, ﴿God turns in forgiveness to whom He wills,﴾ cannot be made a consequence of fighting them against the disbelievers. They said: Its parallel is: ﴿If God wills, He would seal upon your heart﴾ [al-Shura: 24], and the speech ends here. Then He resumed and said: ﴿And God would erase falsehood﴾ [al-Shura: 24]. Some people said: This repentance may be made a consequence of that fighting, and its explanation is from several aspects:

The first: when He commanded them to fight, it may have been hard on some of them, according to what al-Asamm held. So when they advanced to fight, that action takes the place of repentance from that aversion.

The second: the achieving of victory and triumph is a great blessing, and when the servant witnesses the successive blessings of God, it is not unlikely that this becomes a motive for him to repent of all sins.

The third: when victory, triumph, and conquest are attained, and wealth and blessings increase, and his pleasures were being pursued by unlawful means, then, with the attainment of wealth and standing, it becomes possible to obtain them by lawful means, so the abundance of wealth and standing becomes a motive to repent from these matters.

The fourth: some of them said: The soul is strongly inclined to this world and its pleasures. When the doors of this world open to a person, and God intends good for him, he comes to know that its pleasures are base and trivial. Then the world becomes small in his eyes, and this becomes a cause for the soul's withdrawal from the world. This is one of the interpretations mentioned regarding His saying, exalted is He, quoting Solomon, peace be upon him: ﴿Grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾ [Sad: 35]. That is, after the attainment of this kingdom, the soul has no further occupation with seeking the world. Then he knows that upon attaining this kingdom, which is the greatest of kingdoms, there is no real benefit in the world, and no use in its pleasures and desires. At that point the heart turns away from the world and gives it no weight. Thus it is established that the occurrence of fighting leads to the five benefits mentioned, and the attainment of those benefits necessitates repentance, so repentance is connected to that fighting. He said, ﴿on whom He wills,﴾ because the finding of the world and the opening of its doors to a person may become a cause for the heart to withdraw from the world, and that is the case for one for whom God intends good, and it may become a cause for a person to be absorbed in it, to be consumed by it, and to be cut off by it from the path of God. So when the matter varies in the way we have described, He said: ﴿God turns in forgiveness to whom He wills.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And God is Knowing﴾, that is, of everything that is done and performed in His dominion and His kingdom, ﴿Wise﴾, that is, correct in His rulings and His acts.

**Page 6**

The Most High said: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone while Allah had not yet made evident those among you who strove and did not take any intimate associates other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers? And Allah is Acutely Aware of what you do.﴾ Know that the preceding verses were encouraging to jihad, and the purpose of this verse is further clarification in encouragement. It contains several issues:

The first issue: al-Farra' said: His saying ﴿Am﴾ (or) is from the interrogative that occurs in the middle of speech. Had it been intended as a beginning, it would have been with the alif or with it (alone).

The second issue: Abu 'Ubayda said: Anything you insert into something that is not part of it is a *waliyyah* (intimate associate, an insider who is not truly one of the group). Its origin is from *wulūj* (entering). So the one who enters among a people without being one of them is a *waliyyah*. The *waliyyah* is on the pattern of *fa'īlah* from *walaja*, like *dakhīlah* from *dakhala*. Al-Wahidi said: It is said, "He is my *waliyyah*," and "They are my *waliyyah*," for the singular and the plural alike.

The third issue: The purpose of the verse is to explain that the responsible person in this situation is not freed from punishment except when two matters are realized:

The first: that Allah makes evident those among you who strove. Knowledge is mentioned, and what is meant by it is the object of knowledge. The intended meaning is that the jihad proceeds from them. However, since the existence of a thing necessarily entails that its existence is known to Allah, He made His knowledge of its existence a metonym for its existence. Hisham ibn al-Hakam used this verse as evidence that Allah, the Most High, knows a thing only at the time of its existence.

Know that although the apparent meaning of the verse may give the impression of what he mentioned, the intended meaning is what we have explained.

The second: His saying ﴿and did not take any intimate associates other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers﴾. The purpose of mentioning this condition is that a person may engage in jihad without being sincere, and may instead be a hypocrite whose inner state contradicts his outer appearance, and who takes intimate associates other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. So the Most High made clear that He will not leave them alone except when they bring jihad together with sincerity, free from hypocrisy, showing off, cultivating affection for the disbelievers, and nullifying what contradicts the way of the religion. The intended point is that the purpose of enjoining fighting is not merely fighting itself; rather, the purpose is that it be performed in submission to the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to His ruling and obligation, so that through it the expenditure of self and wealth in seeking the good pleasure of Allah, the Most High, becomes manifest. Then benefit is achieved through it. As for undertaking fighting for other aims, that is not beneficial at all.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah is Acutely Aware of what you do﴾, that is: He is knowing of their intentions and aims, aware of them, and nothing of them is hidden from Him. Therefore, a person must strive hard regarding the matter of intention and the guarding of the heart. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Indeed Allah does not approve that the inner state should contradict the outer, and Allah only wants from His creation uprightness, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. He said: When fighting was enjoined, the hypocrite was distinguished from others, and the one who allies with the believers was separated from the one who opposes them.

[Page 7]

**His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while bearing witness against themselves to disbelief. Those—their deeds have become void, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾ ﴿Only one who maintains the mosques of Allah is one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes the prayer, gives the zakah, and fears none but Allah. Perhaps those will be among the guided.﴾

There are several issues in the verse.

**First issue:** He, may He be exalted, began the surah by mentioning disavowal of the disbelievers. He emphasized the obligation of this and mentioned some of their disgraceful and shameful acts that necessitate that disavowal. Then He related doubts by which they argued that this disavowal is not permissible, and that companionship and support must be present. The first of these is what He mentions in this verse. They are described with praiseworthy attributes and commendable qualities, which necessitate associating with them, assisting them, and supporting them. Among these attributes is that they maintained the Sacred Mosque. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: When al-ʿAbbas was taken captive on the Day of Badr, the Muslims approached him and reproached him for his disbelief in Allah and for severing the ties of kinship. ʿAli was harsh with him and said: "Do you have any good deeds?" He said: "Yes, we maintain the Sacred Mosque, we guard the Kaʿbah, we give water to the pilgrims, and we ransom the captive." So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed in reply to al-ʿAbbas: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾

**Second issue:** Maintaining the mosques is of two kinds. Either it means frequenting them and being constant in attending them—one says, "So-and-so maintains the gathering of so-and-so" when he frequents it a great deal—or it means the well-known maintenance of building. If the intended meaning is the second, the meaning is that it is not permissible for a disbeliever to approach the sanctity of the mosques. The reason it is not permissible for him is that the mosque is the place of worship, so it must be honored, whereas the disbeliever demeans it and does not honor it. Also, the disbeliever is ritually impure in legal judgment, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28]. Purifying the mosques is obligatory, based on His saying: ﴿that you purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. Also, the disbeliever does not guard against impurities, so his entering the mosque defiles the mosque, and this may lead to the corruption of the worship of the Muslims. Also, his undertaking the repair of the mosque would amount to a favor done to the Muslims, and it is not permissible for a disbeliever to become one who bestows favor upon the Muslims.

**Third issue:** Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read (أنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ) in the singular, while the rest read ﴿مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ﴾ in the plural. The proof of Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr is His saying: "the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque." The proofs of those who read in the plural form are several:

The first: the intended meaning is the Sacred Mosque, and it is called "mosques" because it is the qiblah of all mosques and their leader, so its maintenance is like the maintenance of all the mosques.

The second: the meaning of ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ is: it is not for the polytheists to maintain any of the mosques of Allah. If that is the case, then it is more fitting that they not be enabled to maintain the Sacred Mosque, which is the most noble and greatest of the mosques.

The third: al-Farraʾ said: The Arabs sometimes place the singular in the position of the plural and the plural in the position of the singular. The placing of the singular in the position of the plural is in their saying: "So-and-so is abundant in dirhams." The placing of the plural in the position of the singular is in their saying: "So-and-so sits with kings," although he sits only with one king.

The fourth: the mosque is the place of prostration, so every part of the Sacred Mosque is a mosque.

**Fourth issue:** al-Wahidi said: The verse indicates that disbelievers are prevented from maintaining any of the mosques of the Muslims. If one of them bequeaths for them, his bequest is not accepted, and he is prevented from entering the mosques. If he enters without the permission of a Muslim, he deserves ta'zir (discretionary punishment). If he enters with permission, he is not punished. The better course is to honor the mosques and keep them away from them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lodged the delegation of Thaqif in the mosque, while they were disbelievers, and he tied Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi to one of the pillars of the Sacred Mosque while he was a disbeliever.

[Page 8]

As for His saying: ﴿bearing witness against themselves to disbelief﴾, al-Zajjaj said: His saying "bearing witness" is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the meaning is: it is not for them to maintain the mosques while they are bearing witness against themselves to disbelief. The commentators mentioned several interpretations of this witness:

The first, which is the most correct, is that they acknowledged against themselves the worship of idols, the denial of the Qur'an, and the rejection of the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). All of these are disbelief. Whoever bears witness against himself to all of these things has borne witness against himself to what is in reality disbelief. The intended meaning is not that they bore witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.

The second: al-Suddi said: Their witness against themselves to disbelief is that when a Christian is asked, "Who are you?" he says, "I am a Christian." The Jew says, "I am a Jew," and the idol-worshiper says, "I am an idol-worshiper." This interpretation is established only by what we have mentioned in the first interpretation.

The third: the extremists among them used to say: "We disbelieve in the religion of Muhammad and in the Qur'an." So perhaps this is what is intended.

The fourth: they used to circumambulate the House naked, saying: "We will not circumambulate upon it in garments in which we have disobeyed Allah." Whenever they completed a circuit, they prostrated to the idols. This is their witness against themselves to polytheism.

The fifth: they used to say: "Here I am, O Allah, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, whom You own and whom he does not own."

The sixth: it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: The intended meaning is that they bear witness against the Messenger with disbelief. He said: This interpretation is permissible because of His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. The Qadi (judge) said: This interpretation is a departure from the literal meaning, and resorting to it is permissible only if it is impossible to apply the expression to its literal meaning. But since we have shown that this is permissible, it is not permissible to resort to this figurative usage (majāz). I say: If one of the early generation had read ﴿bearing witness against themselves to disbelief﴾ from your saying, "Zayd is precious, and ʿAmr is more precious than him," this interpretation would be valid, as a departure from the apparent meaning in it.

Then He said: ﴿Those—their deeds have become void﴾, and what is meant by it is the true judgment in this matter, which is that if any deed of righteousness proceeded from them, such as honoring one's parents, building hospices, feeding the hungry, or honoring a guest, all of that is void, because the punishment for their disbelief exceeds the reward for these things. Thus no effect of any of them remains in deserving reward and honor together with disbelief. As for the discussion of ihbat (nullification of deeds), it has been mentioned in this book many times, so we will not repeat it.

Then He said: ﴿and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾, which is an indication that they will be eternal in the Fire. Our companions (the Ashʿarites) argued with this verse that the sinful person among the people of prayer will not remain eternal in the Fire, for two reasons:

The first: His saying ﴿and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾ conveys restriction, meaning: they, and no others, are the ones who abide in it. Since this statement was addressed concerning the disbelievers, it is established that eternal abiding is attained only by the disbeliever.

The second: He, may He be exalted, made eternal abiding in the Fire the recompense of the disbelievers for their disbelief. If this ruling were established for someone other than the disbelievers, it would not be valid to threaten the disbeliever with it.

Then, when Allah, exalted is He, had explained that the disbeliever has no right to occupy himself with building the mosque, He explained that whoever occupies himself with this work must be described by four attributes.

The first attribute: His saying: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day shall maintain the mosques of Allah﴾. We have said that faith in Allah is indispensable, because the mosque is an expression for the place in which Allah is worshipped; so whoever is not a believer in Allah is prevented from building a place in which Allah is worshipped. And we have said that he must be a believer in Allah and the Last Day, because occupying oneself with the worship of Allah, exalted is He, only benefits in the Hereafter; so whoever denies the Hereafter does not worship Allah, and whoever does not worship Allah does not build a structure for the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

If it is said: Why did He not mention faith in the Messenger of Allah?

We say: In this there are several reasons.

The first: The polytheists used to say: Muhammad only claimed to be the Messenger of Allah in pursuit of leadership and kingship. Here He mentioned faith in Allah and the Last Day and left out prophethood, as if He were saying: My aim from conveying the message is nothing but faith in the Origin and the Return. So He mentioned the primary purpose and omitted the mention of prophethood, as an alert to the disbelievers that he has no aim from the message beyond this measure.

The second: That when He mentioned prayer (al-salah), and prayer is not complete without the adhan, the iqamah and the tashahhud, and these things include mention of prophethood, that was sufficient.

The third: That He mentioned prayer, and the singular noun preceded by the definite article (al-) refers to a previously known referent; the previously known prayer among the Muslims is nothing but the acts which Muhammad ﷺ brought, so the mention of prayer is evidence of prophethood from this angle.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿and establishes prayer﴾. The reason is that the greatest purpose of building mosques is the establishment of the prayers, so a person who does not acknowledge the obligation of the prayers cannot proceed to build mosques.

The third attribute: His saying: ﴿and gives zakah﴾.

Know that the consideration of establishing prayer and paying zakah in the maintenance of the mosque seems to indicate that what is meant by maintaining the mosque is attending it; for when a person establishes prayer, he attends the mosque, so the maintenance of the mosque is achieved by him. And when he pays zakah, groups of poor and needy people attend the mosque seeking to receive zakah, so the maintenance of the mosque is achieved by him. As for if we take "maintenance" to mean the interests of construction, then paying zakah is also considered in this matter, because paying zakah is obligatory, and building a mosque is voluntary (nafilah), and a person does not occupy himself with the voluntary until he is free from the obligatory. And it is apparent that a person who is not paying zakah does not occupy himself with building mosques.

The fourth attribute: His saying: ﴿and fears none but Allah﴾. And concerning it there are several reasons:

The first: That Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, built at the beginning of Islam a mosque at the door of his house, and he used to pray in it and recite the Qur'an, while the disbelievers harmed him because of it. It is possible that what is meant is that situation, meaning: even if people feared building the mosque, he did not heed them nor fear them, but he built the mosque out of fear of Allah, exalted is He.

The second: It is possible that what is meant by it is that he builds the mosque not for the sake of showing off and reputation, so that it is said: So-and-so is building a mosque; rather he builds it solely seeking the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He, and solely to strengthen the religion of Allah.

If it is said: How can He say ﴿and fears none but Allah﴾ when the believer may fear oppressors and corrupters?

We say: What is meant by this fear is fear and piety in matters of religion, and that one does not prefer the pleasure of anyone else over the pleasure of Allah.

Know that He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah﴾, i.e., whoever is described by these four attributes. The word ﴿إنما﴾ (innama, "only") indicates restriction, and in it there is an alert that the mosque must be kept free from anything other than worship, so idle talk and the handling of worldly affairs are included in this. And from the Prophet ﷺ: "In the last age there will come people from my ummah who come to the mosques and sit in them in circles, their remembrance is the world and love of the world; do not sit with them, for Allah has no need of them." And in a hadith: "Talk in the mosque devours good deeds as the beast devours grass." The peace and blessings of Allah be upon him said: "Allah, exalted is He, said: 'Indeed My houses on earth are the mosques, and those who visit Me in them are their inhabitants. Blessed is the servant who purifies himself in his house, then visits Me in My house; it is a right upon the one visited to honour his visitor.'" And from him, peace be upon him: "Whoever becomes attached to the mosque, Allah becomes attached to him." And from him, peace be upon him: "When you see a man frequenting the mosque, bear witness to his faith." And from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever lights a lamp in a mosque, the angels and the bearers of the Throne will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as its light remains in the mosque." These hadiths were transmitted by the author of al-Kashshaf.

Then, when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned these attributes, He said: ﴿So it is expected that those will be among the guided﴾. And concerning it there are several views:

The first: The exegetes said: "Expectation (ʿasā)" from Allah is binding, because He is exalted above doubt and hesitation.

The second: Abu Muslim said: "ʿasā" here refers to the servants, and it indicates hope; so the meaning is that those who perform these acts of obedience perform them in hope of attaining guidance, based on His saying: ﴿They call upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾ [al-Sajdah: 16]. The verification in this is that the servant, when performing these deeds, does not decisively claim attainment of reward, because he allows for himself that he may have failed in one of the conditions that are required for acceptance.

The third, which is the best of the views: what the author of al-Kashshaf mentioned, namely that what is meant by it is to distance the polytheists from the positions of guidance and to cut off their hopes of benefiting from their deeds, which they regarded as great and boasted of. For Allah, exalted is He, explained that those who believed and joined to their faith the practice of the laws and joined to them the fear of Allah, for these people the attainment of guidance has become subject to "perhaps" and "expectation." So what is the matter with these polytheists that they claim with certainty that they are guided and firmly assert their success in good from Allah, exalted is He? In this statement and its like there is kindness to the believers in preferring fear over hope.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: The exegetes have mentioned several reports concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, in some of the reports from him, said: When 'Ali spoke harshly to al-'Abbas, al-'Abbas said: "If you have preceded us in Islam, emigration (hijrah) and jihad, then we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque and give water to the pilgrims," so this verse was revealed. It is also said that the polytheists said to the Jews: "We are the providers of water for the pilgrims and the maintainers of the Sacred Mosque; so are we better, or Muhammad and his companions?" The Jews said to them: "You are better." It is also said: "'Ali, peace be upon him, said to al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, after his conversion to Islam: 'O my uncle, will you not emigrate? Will you not join the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' He said: 'Am I not in a position better than emigration? I give water to the pilgrims of the House of Allah and maintain the Sacred Mosque.' When this verse was revealed, he said: 'I see myself only as one who abandons our providing of water,' and the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, said: 'Continue in your providing of water, for there is good for you in it.'" It is also said: Talhah ibn Shaybah, al-'Abbas and 'Ali boasted. Talhah said: "I am the keeper of the House; its key is in my hand, and if I wished I could spend the night in it." al-'Abbas said: "I am the keeper of the water-providing and in charge of it." 'Ali said: "I am the one who strives (in jihad)." So Allah revealed this verse.

The author, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The summary of the matter is that it is possible to say that this verse is a comparison that took place among the Muslims, and it is possible that it took place between the Muslims and the disbelievers. As for those who said that it took place among the Muslims, they argued by His saying, exalted is He, after this verse, concerning the believing emigrants: ﴿They are greater in rank with Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 20]. This also implies that the one who is inferior has a rank with Allah too, and that does not befit anyone but a believer. We will answer this argument when we reach it. As for those who said:

Page 11
that it took place between the Muslims and the disbelievers, they argued for the soundness of their view by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as one who believes in Allah﴾, and by the specification of who believes in Allah. This, in my view, is the closer position.

The explanation of the matter: We have already transmitted, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Only he who believes in Allah maintains the mosques of Allah﴾, that al-'Abbas argued for his own merits by saying that he maintained the Sacred Mosque and gave water to the pilgrims, and Allah answered him with two aspects:

The first aspect: What was explained in the first verse, that the maintenance of the mosque only brings merit when it proceeds from a believer; as for when it proceeds from a disbeliever, there is absolutely no benefit in it.

The second aspect of the answer: Everything mentioned in this verse, namely that one may say: Suppose we concede that maintaining the Sacred Mosque and giving water to the pilgrims does bring some kind of merit, yet in comparison to belief in Allah and jihad it is very little. So mentioning these deeds in opposition to belief in Allah and jihad is an error, because it implies setting the very noble and exalted thing against the very base and trivial thing, and that is invalid. This is the way to understand this verse, and by this route the verse coheres correctly with what precedes it.

The second issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: al-siqayah (providing water) and al-'imarah (maintenance) are verbal nouns (masdar) from saqa and 'amara, like al-siyanah and al-wiqayah.

Know that "providing water" and "maintenance" are actions, while His saying, "one who believes in Allah," refers to an agent. The apparent wording thus requires likening an action to an agent, and an attribute to a substance, which is impossible; so an interpretation is necessary, and it is of two kinds:

The first: We say the implied meaning is: "Do you consider the people of providing water for the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in Allah?" This is strengthened by the reading of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: (suqat al-hajj wa-'amarat al-Masjid al-Haram).

The second: We say the implied meaning is: "Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims as equal to the belief of one who believes in Allah?" A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177] up to His saying: ﴿But righteousness is one who believes in Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177].

The third issue: al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The providing of water was with raisin nabidh (nabidh al-zabib). It is reported from 'Umar that he found the raisin nabidh of the providing of water strong, so he diluted it with water three times, and said: "If it becomes strong upon you, dilute it with water."

As for the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque, what is meant is equipping it and beautifying the appearance of its walls. When Allah mentioned the description of the two groups, He said: ﴿They are not equal﴾. But since denying equality between them does not indicate which of them is superior, He drew attention to the superior one by His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Thus He made clear that the disbelievers are wrongdoers to themselves, for they were created for faith, yet they were content with disbelief and became wrongdoers; for wrongdoing (zulm) is an expression for placing a thing in other than its proper place. Also, they wronged the Sacred Mosque, for Allah, exalted is He, created it to be a place for the worship of Allah, exalted is He, and they made it a place for the worship of idols, and this was wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with God. And those are the ones who are the victorious.﴾ ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, approval, and gardens for them wherein is lasting pleasure.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein forever. Indeed, with God is a great reward.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned the preference of faith and jihad over giving water to pilgrims (al-siqayah) and the upkeep of the Sacred Mosque (imarat al-Masjid al-Haram), by way of allusion. Then He followed it with a mention of this preference explicitly in this verse, saying: whoever is described by these four attributes is greater in rank with God than one who is characterized by giving water and maintaining the mosque. These four attributes are these:

The first of them: faith.

The second: emigration (hijrah).

The third: jihad in the cause of God with wealth.

The fourth: jihad with the self.

We have said that those described by these four attributes are at the utmost height of majesty and elevation, because a human being possesses only a collection of three things: the spirit, the body, and wealth. As for the spirit, when disbelief is removed from it and faith is established in it, it has attained the levels of happiness appropriate to it.

As for the body and wealth, through emigration they fall into deficiency, and through engaging in jihad they become exposed to destruction and ruin. There is no doubt that the self and wealth are beloved to a person, and a person does not turn away from what he loves except to obtain something beloved that is more perfect than the first. Had seeking the good pleasure (ridwan) not been more complete for them than self and wealth, they would not have preferred the side of the Hereafter over the side of self and wealth, nor would they have agreed to squander self and wealth in seeking the pleasure of God, exalted is He. Thus it is established that when the four attributes are attained, the person reaches the last of the degrees of humanity and the first of the degrees of the angels. And what relation is there between this rank and undertaking the giving of water and the upkeep of the mosque merely by imitating the fathers and forebears, or by seeking leadership and reputation?

By this certain proof, the correctness of His saying, exalted is He, is established: ﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with God. And those are the ones who are the victorious.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, did not say "greater in rank than those occupied with giving water and maintaining the mosque," because if He had specified them, it would have implied that their virtue was attained in relation to them. And since He omitted mention of the lesser, this indicates that they are superior to everyone else absolutely, because it is not conceivable that a person could attain a happiness and virtue higher and more perfect than these attributes.

Know that His saying ﴿with God﴾ indicates that what is meant by the servant being "with God" is total immersion in his servitude and obedience, and what is not meant is nearness in terms of direction or place. At this point it becomes clear that just as the angels attained the distinction of nearness in His saying: ﴿And those who are with Him do not disdain from His worship﴾ [al-Anbiya’: 19], so too the holy human spirits, when they are purified from the filth of bodily attributes and the corporeal impurities, shine with the lights of majesty, the radiance of the world of perfection is manifested in them, and they ascend from servanthood to nearness. Indeed, there is no perfection in servanthood except witnessing the reality of nearness; for this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra’: 1].

If it is said: since you have stated that these attributes existed among both Muslims and disbelievers, how then does He say of them: ﴿those are greater in rank,﴾ when the disbelievers have no rank at all?

We say: the answer to this is in several respects:

The first: this came in accordance with what they used to estimate for themselves of rank and virtue with God. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate with Him?﴾ [al-Naml: 59], and His saying: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ [al-Saffat: 62].

The second: what is meant may be: "those are greater in rank than everyone who was not described by these

Page 13

attributes," as an alert that since they were more excellent than the believers who were not described by these attributes, then they should not be compared with the disbelievers, a fortiori.

The third: what is meant may be that the believing, emigrating, struggling person is more excellent than the one occupied with giving water and maintaining the mosque, and what is intended is the preference of those deeds over these deeds. There is no doubt that giving water and maintaining the mosque are among the deeds of goodness, and their being made meritorious was only nullified with respect to the disbelievers, because the persistence of disbelief, which is the greatest of crimes, prevents the manifestation of that effect.

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that those described by faith and emigration are greater in rank with God, He explained that they are ﴿the victorious.﴾ This is for restriction (hasr), and the meaning is that they are the ones who are victorious with the lofty, noble, sanctified rank to which reference was made by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with God,﴾ and it is the rank of nearness. That is because whoever believes in God and knows Him, his heart rarely remains inclined toward this world. Then at this point he seeks to remove this knot from the essence of the spirit, and the removal of love of this world is not completed for him except by separating the self from the pleasures of this world. When that separation continues and his attachment to love of this world diminishes, this separation and diminishment are achieved through emigration. Then after that there must necessarily be the belittling of this world and the recognition of its defects, and its becoming, in the eye of the intelligent person, such that he obligates himself to abandon and reject it. This is only completed through jihad, because it is exposing self and wealth to destruction and ruin; and had he not belittled this world, he would not have done that. At this point, what some of the verifiers (muhaqqiqun) have said is fulfilled, namely that gnosis (irfan) begins with separation, diminishment, abandonment, and rejection. Then when this state is attained, the heart becomes occupied with contemplating the attributes of majesty and honor, and in witnessing them there occurs the giving of self and wealth. Thus the person becomes a witness (shahid), beholding the world of majesty, illumined by the light of majesty, and is testified to by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, approval, and gardens for them wherein is lasting pleasure,﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever.﴾ At this point the arrival at the presence of the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Ahad al-Samad) is attained, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿with God.﴾ Here it is fitting to stop at the point of arrival.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him, and of approval, and of gardens for them wherein is lasting bliss.﴾ ﴿Therein they will abide forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward.﴾

Know that this indication includes several kinds of lofty ranks, and that He, exalted is He, began with the most noble and then the most noble, descending to the lesser and then the lesser. We will explain it at one time according to the method of the theologians (mutakallimun) and at another according to the method of the gnostics (arifun).

As for the first, we say: The first rank among them, which is the highest and most noble, is that this good news comes from their Lord with mercy and approval, and this is glorification and honor from the side of God. His saying ﴿and gardens for them﴾ indicates the attainment of great benefits, and His saying ﴿wherein is bliss﴾ indicates that the benefits are pure, free from troubles, for bliss (naʿim) is an intensification of blessing (niʿmah), and there is no meaning to intensifying blessing except that it is free from being mixed with turbidity. His saying ﴿lasting (muqim)﴾ is an expression of their being enduring and uninterrupted. Then He, exalted is He, expressed their permanence by three expressions:

The first: ﴿lasting (muqim)﴾.

The second: His saying ﴿therein they abide (khalidina fiha)﴾.

The third: His saying ﴿forever (abadan)﴾.

From the totality of what we have mentioned, it results that He, exalted is He, gives good news to these believers, the emigrants and the strivers, of a benefit that is pure, lasting, and joined with glorification, and that is the definition of reward. The purpose of singling out these believers so that this reward is of complete degree and high rank is according to each one of these four restrictions. Among the theologians is one who said: His saying ﴿their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him﴾ means the goods of this world; His saying ﴿and of approval and gardens﴾ means that He is pleased with them while they are in this worldly life; His saying ﴿and gardens﴾ means the benefits; and His saying ﴿for them therein is bliss﴾ means that those blessings are

Page 14
pure from troubles, for bliss is an intensification of blessing; and His saying ﴿lasting﴾ and ﴿therein they abide forever﴾ means the glorification and honor that must be attained in reward.

As for the explanation of this verse according to the method of the gnostic lovers who yearn, we say: The first of the matters mentioned in this verse is His saying ﴿their Lord gives them good news﴾.

Know that joy in a blessing falls into two types:

One: that one rejoices in the blessing because it is a blessing.

The second: that one rejoices in it not for its own sake but because the Benefactor singled him out with it and honored him. If your mind is unable to reach the distinction between the two types, then reflect on the case of a servant standing in the presence of the greatest sultan while the other servants stand in his service; when that sultan throws an apple to one of those servants, that servant's joy is greatly increased. That great joy did not arise from the arrival of that apple, but from the fact that the sultan singled him out with that honor. So it is here.

His saying ﴿their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him and of approval﴾: among them are those whose joy is due to attaining that mercy, and among them are those who do not rejoice in attaining that mercy but rejoice only because their Master singled them out with that mercy; in that case his joy is not in the mercy but in the One who bestowed the mercy. Then this station also has degrees: among them is one whose joy is in the Merciful, because He showed mercy; and among them is one who penetrates deeply into sincerity and forgets the mercy, and his joy is only in the Master, because He is the goal. That is because as long as the servant is occupied with the Truth in terms of Him being Merciful, he is not wholly absorbed in the Truth, but at times with the Truth and at times with creation. When the matter is complete, he is cut off from creation, drowns in the sea of the light of the Truth, and becomes oblivious to love and trial, to vengeance and blessing, to affliction and favors. The realized ones (al-muhaqqiqun) stopped at His saying ﴿their Lord gives them good news﴾, so their gladness, their delight in it, their reliance upon it, and their return to it were in this. Among them is one who has not reached that lofty degree, so his soul is satisfied only with the whole of His saying ﴿their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him﴾; he does not know that the delight at hearing the word of their Lord, but rather he rejoices in the totality of being given good news of mercy.

The second rank: that his delight be in the mercy. This rank is the lower one according to the realized ones. The second subtlety of this verse is that He, exalted is He, said ﴿their Lord gives them good news﴾, and it includes several kinds of mercy and honor:

First: that good news is only given with mercy and kindness.

Second: that the good news given to each person must be fitting to his condition. Since the one giving the good news here is the Most Generous of the generous, the good news must be of goods that minds are unable to describe and understandings fall short of depicting.

Third: that He, exalted is He, named Himself here as "the Lord (Rabb)", which is derived from "upbringing (tarbiyah)", as if He said: the One who raised you in this world with blessings that have no limit or count, gives you good news of lofty goods and complete felicities.

Fourth: that He, exalted is He, said ﴿their Lord﴾, attributing Himself to them, and did not attribute them to Himself.

Fifth: that He, exalted is He, placed their mention before the mention of Himself, saying ﴿He gives them good news, their Lord﴾.

Sixth: that good news is the report of the occurrence of something whose occurrence was not known; if its occurrence were already known, it would not be good news. Do you not see that the jurists said: if a man says, "Whichever of my slaves brings me news of the arrival of my son, he is free," then the first one to report that news is freed, and those who report after him are not freed. Since the matter is so, His saying ﴿He gives them good news﴾ must be an announcement of the attainment of a rank of felicities which they did not know before. All the delights, goods, and pleasures of Paradise they had already known in this world from the Qur'an; so the announcement of the attainment of good news must be good news of felicities that minds cannot reach to describe at all. May Allah, exalted is He, grant us the attainment of them by His grace and generosity.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever among you allies with them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾

Know that the purpose of mentioning this verse is that it should be a reply to another doubt that they raised concerning whether disassociation (al-bara'ah) from the disbelievers is possible. That doubt was that they said: a Muslim man may have a disbelieving father, and a disbelieving man may have a father or brother who is a Muslim, and complete severance between a man and his father and brother is something difficult and impossible. Since this is the case, the disassociation that God commanded would be a burdensome and impossible thing. So God, may He be exalted, mentioned this verse to remove this doubt. Al-Wahidi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: When the believers were commanded to emigrate (hijrah) before the conquest of Mecca, whoever did not emigrate, God would not accept his faith until he cut off from his fathers and relatives if they were disbelievers. The author, may God be pleased with him, said: This is problematic, because the correct view is that this surah was revealed only after the conquest of Mecca, so how can this verse be understood in the way they have stated? The closer view in my opinion is that it should be understood in the sense I have mentioned, namely that when God commanded the believers to disassociate from the polytheists and emphasized its obligation, they said: how can this complete severance be possible between a man and his father, his mother, and his brother? So God, may He be exalted, mentioned that severance from fathers, children and brothers is obligatory because of disbelief, which is His saying: ﴿if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾. And istihbab (preferring) means seeking love, as one says: istahabba lahu, meaning he loved him, as if he sought his love. Then, after forbidding them from associating with them, and since the wording of the prohibition could be a prohibition of reprehension (nahy tanzih) or a prohibition of unlawfulness (nahy tahrim), He mentioned what removes the doubt, saying: ﴿And whoever among you allies with them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He means one who is a polytheist like them, because he is pleased with their polytheism, and being pleased with disbelief is disbelief, just as being pleased with sinfulness is sinfulness. The judge (al-Qadi) said: This prohibition does not prevent a person from disassociating from his father in this world, just as it does not prevent him from paying the debt of a disbeliever or employing him in his affairs.

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 9, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce you fear will decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Know that this verse is a confirmation of the answer mentioned in the first verse. This is because a group of the believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is it possible to disavow them completely? This disavowal requires us to cut ties with our fathers, our brothers and our kinsfolk, the loss of our trade, the destruction of our wealth, the ruin of our homes, and leaving us in ruin." So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that it is necessary to bear all these worldly harms so that the religion may remain sound. He mentioned that if the protection of these worldly interests is more important to you than obedience to Allah and His Messenger and striving in the way of Allah, then wait with what you love until Allah brings His command, that is, a punishment, either swift or delayed. The purpose of this is a warning.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾, that is, those who step outside His obedience into disobedience to Him. This is also a threat. This verse indicates that if a conflict arises between one of the interests of the religion and all the важных matters of this world, then it is obligatory for the Muslim to prefer the religion over the world. Al-Wahidi (Wahidi) said: His saying, ﴿and your kinsfolk (ʿashīratukum)﴾: the ʿashīrah of a man is his nearest family, those who associate closely with him. Abu Bakr, from Asim, read (wa-ʿashīrātukum) in the plural, while the rest read it in the singular. As for the one who reads it in the plural, this is because each one of the addressees has a ʿashīrah, so when you pluralize it you say ʿashīrāt. As for the one who reads it in the singular, he says: the word ʿashīrah applies to the plural, so it dispenses with its plural form. This is strengthened by the statement of al-Akhfash (al-Akhfash): the Arabs hardly ever pluralize ʿashīrah as ʿashīrāt; rather, they pluralize it as ʿashāʾir. His saying, ﴿and wealth you have acquired (iqtaraftumūhā)﴾: iqtirāf means acquisition.

Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned the matters that prompt mixing with the disbelievers, and these are four matters:

The first: association with relatives. He mentioned four categories of them in detail, namely fathers, sons, brothers and spouses. Then He mentioned the rest with a single term that encompasses all of them, which is the term ʿashīrah.

The second: the inclination to hold on to acquired wealth.

The third: the desire to gain wealth through trade.

The fourth: the desire for dwellings. There is no doubt that this ordering is a good ordering, for the greatest of the causes that prompt association is kinship. Then through that association one reaches the preservation of wealth already possessed. Then through association one reaches the acquisition of wealth that is not yet possessed. And at the last of these levels is the desire to build in homelands and houses that were built for the purpose of dwelling. So Allah, exalted is He, mentioned these things in this required order, and He made clear at the end that protecting the religion is better than protecting all of these matters.

[Page 17]

The Exalted said: ﴿Allah had already given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number made you vain, but it availed you nothing. The earth, spacious as it is, became too narrow for you, and then you turned back in retreat. Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers. Then after that, Allah turns in forgiveness to whomever He wills, and Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

On this verse there are several issues.

The first issue: Know that in the preceding verse He mentioned that it is obligatory to turn away from associating with fathers, sons, brothers, and kin, and from wealth, trade, and dwellings, for the sake of the interests of the religion. When Allah knew that this is very difficult for souls and hearts, He mentioned what shows that whoever leaves the world for the sake of the religion, Allah will also bring him to what he seeks from the world. The Exalted gave an example of this: the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the battle of Hunayn was at the height of its number and strength. When they were made vain by their numbers, they became routed. Then, in the state of their rout, when they humbled themselves before Allah, He strengthened them until they defeated the army of the disbelievers. This shows that whenever a person relies on the world, he loses both the religion and the world, and whenever he obeys Allah and prefers the religion over the world, Allah gives him both the religion and the world in the best manner. So the mention of this was a consolation for those whom Allah had commanded to cut off fathers, sons, wealth, and dwellings for the sake of the interest of the religion, and a means of making them patient with it, and a promise to them by way of allusion: that if they do that, Allah will bring them to their relatives, their wealth, and their dwellings in the best manner. This is the explanation of the structure (nazm) of the verse, and it is of the utmost excellence.

The second issue: al-Wahidi said: "Naṣr" (victory) is help against the enemy specifically. "Mawāṭin" is the plural of "mawṭin," which is every place where a person stays for a matter. Accordingly, "mawāṭin al-ḥarb" are its stations and positions. Its being non-diptote (not taking tanwin) is because it is a plural in a form that has no singular of its pattern. The "many battlefields" are the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah, and it is said that they were eighty battlefields. Allah the Exalted informed them that it is He who gave the believers victory, and whomever Allah gives victory, no one can overcome him.

Then He said: ﴿and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number made you vain﴾, meaning: remember the day of Hunayn, among those battlefields, when your great number made you vain.

The third issue: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Mecca, and some days of the month of Ramadan remained, he set out heading for Hunayn to fight Hawazin and Thaqif. They differed about the number of the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ata reported from Ibn Abbas: they were sixteen thousand. Qatada said: they were twelve thousand, ten thousand of those who had been present at Mecca and two thousand of the Tulaqa' (those freed at the conquest). Al-Kalbi said: they were ten thousand. In sum, they were a large number. Hawazin and Thaqif were four thousand. When the two sides met, a man from the Muslims said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." This statement displeased the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it is what is meant by His saying: ﴿when your great number made you vain﴾. It was also said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself said it, and it was said that Abu Bakr said it. But attributing this statement to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is far-fetched, because in most circumstances he was reliant upon Allah, with his heart detached from the world and its causes.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 27:

Then the Exalted said: ﴿So it did not avail you at all﴾. The meaning of ighna' (granting sufficiency) is giving what removes need. So His saying ﴿it did not avail you at all﴾ means: it did not give you anything that removes your need. The purpose of this statement is that God Most High informed them that they would not be overcome by their great numbers, but are only overcome by the help of God. So when they were impressed by their numbers, they became defeated. His saying ﴿and the earth, for all its vastness, was confining for you﴾: it is said raha, yarhu, rahban wa-rahabatan (rahuba: to be wide/vast). So His saying ﴿bima rahubat﴾ means "with its vastness," and its meaning is "together with its vastness." Here ma (in "bima") with the verb functions as a verbal noun (masdar). The meaning is: because of the intensity of the fear that befell you, the earth became confining for you, so you did not find in it a place suitable for your flight from your enemy. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: "Hawazin were archers. When we charged against them, they were routed, and we fell upon the spoils, and they met us with arrows, and the Muslims fled from the Messenger of God ﷺ, and there remained with him only al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith." Al-Bara' said: "By Him besides whom there is no god, the Messenger of God ﷺ never turned his back at all." He said: "And I saw him, and Abu Sufyan was holding the stirrup, and al-'Abbas was holding the bridle of his mount, and he was saying: 'I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib.' And he began to urge his mule toward the disbelievers, heedless, and his mule was grey-white. Then he said to al-'Abbas: 'Call the Emigrants and the Helpers.' Al-'Abbas was a man of loud voice, so he began calling: 'O servants of God! O companions of the tree! O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!' The Muslims came, when they heard his voice, as one body. The Messenger of God ﷺ took a handful of pebbles, threw them at them, and said: 'Ugly be the faces!' Their affair then kept turning back, and their edge became blunted, until God Most High defeated them, and none of them that day remained without his eyes being filled with that dust." That is His saying: ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾.

Know that when the Most High explained that multitude does not benefit, and that what necessitated victory was nothing but from God, He mentioned three matters:

The first: the sending down of tranquility (sakinah). Sakinah is that in which the heart and the soul find rest, and it brings security and calm. I think the aspect of metaphor in it is that when a person fears he flees while his heart is agitated, and when he feels secure he settles and stays firm. Since security necessitates stillness, the word sakinah was used as a metaphor (kinayah) for security.

Know that His saying ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ indicates that the act depends on the arising of the motive, and indicates that the arising of the motive is only from God Most High.

As for the explanation of the first: when the people were routed, the motive of calm and steadfastness did not arise in their hearts, so calm and steadfastness did not occur, but the people fled and were defeated. When the tranquility, which is an expression for the motive of calm and steadfastness, arose, they returned to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and stood firm with him and became calm. This shows that the occurrence of the act depends on the occurrence of the motive.

As for the explanation of the second: that the arising of that motive is from God Most High is explicit.

His saying: ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger﴾. Reason also indicates it: if the arising of that motive in the heart were from the servant, it would depend on the arising of another motive, and that would lead to an infinite regress, which is impossible.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And He sent down armies you did not see﴾. Know that this is the second matter that God did on that day. There is no disagreement that what is meant is the sending down of angels. The apparent text does not indicate the number of angels, as is mentioned in the story of Badr. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: God aided His Prophet with five thousand angels, and perhaps he mentioned this number by analogy with the Day of Badr. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: A man who was among the polytheists on the Day of Hunayn told me, he said: "When we routed the Muslims, we began driving them, and when we reached the owner of the grey-white mule, men with bright faces and handsome appearance met us, and they said: 'Ugly be the faces! Return!' So we returned, and they rode upon our shoulders." Also they differed as to whether the angels fought on that day. The report we have transmitted from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab indicates that they fought. Some said: the angels did not fight except on the Day of Badr. As for the benefit of their descent on this day, it is the casting of good thoughts into the hearts of the believers.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾. This is the third matter that the Messenger of God ﷺ did on that day. What is meant by this punishment is their killing and capture, the seizure of their wealth, and the taking captive of their offspring. Our companions (the Ash'arites) argued by this that the act of the servant is the creation of God, because what is meant by punishment is nothing but seizure and capture, and He Most High attributed those things to Himself. We have already shown that His saying ﴿Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger﴾ indicates this, so the combination of these two statements becomes a clear, established proof. On this question the Mu'tazilah said: He Most High attributed that act to Himself only because it occurred by His command, and its answer has been given more than once.

Then He said: ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾. What is meant is that this punishment is the recompense of the disbelievers. Know that the people of the haqiqah (the realists/jurists of the ultimate reality) relied, in the question of flogging combined with ta'zir (discretionary punishment), on His saying: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each of them﴾ [al-Nur: 2]. They said: the fa' indicates that the flogging is a recompense (jaza'), and jaza' is a name for what suffices, and that the flogging being sufficient prevents other punishment from being prescribed along with it. We answer this by saying: jaza' is not a name for what suffices; this is because He Most High named this punishment a recompense, while the Muslims unanimously agreed that the everlasting punishment in the Hereafter is stored up for them. So this verse indicates that jaza' is not a name for what achieves sufficiency.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Then God turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills﴾. He means: despite all the humiliation that befell them, God Most High may still turn in forgiveness toward them. Our companions said: He Most High may turn toward some of them by removing disbelief from their hearts and creating Islam in them. The qadi (al-Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar) said: its meaning is that after what befell them, when they embrace Islam and repent, God Most High accepts their repentance. This is weak, because His saying ﴿Then God turns in forgiveness﴾ apparently indicates that this repentance occurred for them from God Most High. The complete discussion of this meaning is mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah in His saying: (then He turned to him in forgiveness).

Then He said: ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., Forgiving to whoever repents, Merciful to whoever believes and does righteous deeds. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are but impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

Regarding the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that this is the third doubt that fell into the hearts of the people. That is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded ʿAli to recite to the polytheists of Makkah the beginning of Surah Bara'ah, and to announce to them the termination of their covenant, and that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation to the polytheists, some people said: "O people of Makkah, you will know the hardship you will face because of the cutting off of the roads and the loss of the camel-loads (of trade)." So this verse was revealed to repel this doubt, and Allah, exalted is He, answered it with His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, meaning destitution and need, ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. This is the coherence (nazm) of the verse, and it is good and fitting.

The second issue: Most scholars said the word "polytheists" (mushrikin) covers the worshippers of idols. Others said rather it covers all disbelievers. This question has already been discussed, and we established this view with many proofs. What is useful here is to hold to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa: 48]. And it is known that this is false.

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: najas is a verbal noun from najisa najasan and qadhira qadharan, and its meaning is "possessing impurity." Al-Layth said: najas is a thing that is filthy, of people and of everything; a man is najis, a people are anjas, and another dialect says a man is najis, a people are nujs, and so-and-so is najis, a man is najas and a woman is najas. They differed in explaining the polytheist being najas. The author of al-Kashshaf reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that their very bodies are impure like dogs and pigs, and from al-Hasan that whoever shakes hands with a polytheist must perform ablution. This is the view of al-Hadi, one of the imams of the Zaydiyyah. As for the jurists, they agreed on the purity of their bodies.

Know that the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that they are impure, so it is not to be turned away from except by a separate proof. The claim of consensus on it cannot be made, because we have shown that disagreement on it exists. Al-Qadi argued for their purity by what is reported: that the Prophet (ﷺ) drank from their vessels; and also, if their bodies were impure, that would not have been changed by means of Islam. Those who hold the first view answered him: the Qur'an is stronger than a single-report (khabar al-wahid). Also, even granting the soundness of the report, it must be believed that permission to drink from their vessels preceded the revelation of this verse. Its explanation is in two ways:

First: this surah is among the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an. Also, mixing with the disbelievers had been permitted, and Allah prohibited it; treaties with them existed, and Allah removed them. So it is not far-fetched to say also that drinking from their vessels was permitted, and Allah prohibited it.

Second: the original ruling is permissibility of drinking from any vessel. So if we say it was prohibited by the ruling of the verse and then made lawful again by the ruling of the report, two abrogations occur. But if we say it was lawful not by the original ruling, while the Messenger drank from their vessels by the original ruling, and then the prohibition came by the ruling of this verse, abrogation has occurred only once, so this is more preferable. As for al-Qadi's saying: "If the disbeliever's body were impure, the impurity would not be changed to purity by means of Islam," the answer is that this is analogy against an explicit text. Also, the proponents of this view say that when a disbeliever becomes Muslim he must perform ghusl to remove the impurity arising from the ruling of disbelief. This is the statement of this view. As for the majority of jurists, they ruled that the disbeliever is pure in his body, and then they differed in interpreting this verse in several ways:

First: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: its meaning is that they do not perform ghusl from major impurity, nor perform wudu from minor impurity.

Second: the intended meaning is that they are in the position of a najis thing in the obligation of avoiding it.

Third: their disbelief, which is an attribute of them, is in the position of impurity clinging to a thing.

Know that all these interpretations are departures from the apparent meaning without any proof.

* * *

The fourth issue: Abu Hanifah and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: the limbs of one who is in a state of minor impurity (muhdith) are najis with a ruling-based impurity (najasah hukmiyyah), and on this they built the ruling that water used in wudu and in ghusl from major impurity is najis. Then Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him, reported that it is najis with a light impurity; al-Hasan ibn Ziyad reported that it is najis with a heavy impurity; and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported that this water is pure.

Know that His saying: ﴿the polytheists are but impure﴾ shows the corruption of this view, because the particle innama is for restriction, and this requires that there is no impurity except the polytheist. So the claim that the limbs of one in minor impurity are najis contradicts this text. And it is strange that this text is explicit that the polytheist is impure and that the believer is not impure. Then some people reversed the matter and said: the polytheist is pure, and the believer, while in minor or major impurity, is impure. They claimed that the waters that polytheists used on their limbs remain pure and purifying, while the waters with which the greatest prophets used on their limbs are najis with heavy impurity. This is one of the wonders. What further confirms the view of the purity of the Muslim's limbs is his saying, peace be upon him: "The believer does not become impure, alive or dead." So this report agrees with the Qur'an. Then the rulings derived by reasoning agree with the Qur'an and the reports on this matter, because the Muslims agreed that if a person carries one in minor impurity during his prayer, his prayer is not invalidated, even if his hand were wet and it reached the hand of one in minor impurity, his hand does not become najis; and if one in minor impurity sweats and that dampness reaches his garment, that garment does not become najis. So the Qur'an, the report and consensus agree on the view of the purity of the limbs of one in minor impurity; how then can it be opposed? The objection of the opponent is that wudu is called purification (tahara), and purification is only after prior impurity. This is weak, because the word tahara is used for removing sins and offences. Allah, exalted is He, said concerning the people of the house: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House, and to purify you with complete purification﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 33], and this purification is nothing but from sins and offences. And He said concerning Mary: ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen you and purified you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 42], and what is meant is her purification from false accusation.

Since this is established, we say: the sound reports have come that wudu is the purification of the limbs from sins and offences. When the Lawgiver explained wudu as purification in this sense, what then compelled us to oppose it and to go to something that nullifies the Qur'an, the reports, and the consensual rulings?

* * *

The fifth issue: al-Shafiʿi, may Allah be pleased with him, said: disbelievers are prevented from al-Masjid al-Haram specifically. According to Malik, they are prevented from all mosques. According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, they are not prevented from al-Masjid al-Haram nor from the rest of the mosques. The verse by its explicit wording invalidates the view of Abu Hanifah, and by its implicit meaning invalidates the view of Malik. Or we say: the original state is non-prevention, and we departed from it regarding al-Masjid al-Haram by this explicit and decisive text, so it remains in other places in accordance with the original state.

The sixth issue: They differed over whether the intended meaning of al-Masjid al-Haram is the mosque itself or the whole Haram. The closer view is the second, and the proof for it is His saying: ﴿and if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. That is because the place of trade is not the mosque itself; so if the intended meaning of this verse were prohibition from the mosque specifically, they would not have feared poverty because of this prohibition. They only fear poverty if they are prevented from attending the markets and seasonal fairs. This is a good inference from the verse. This view is reinforced by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa﴾ [Al-Isra: 1], although they all agreed that the Messenger, peace be upon him, was lifted from the house of Umm Hani. Also, this is reinforced by what is reported from the Messenger (ﷺ) that he said: "Two religions do not gather in the Arabian Peninsula."

Know that our companions said: the Haram is forbidden to the polytheists. If the imam is in Makkah and the envoy of the polytheists comes, he should go out to the outskirts (al-Hill) to hear the message. If a polytheist enters the Haram secretly and falls ill there, we take him out while he is sick. If he dies and is buried and it is not known, we dig him up and remove his bones if possible.

* * *

The seventh issue: There is no doubt that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿after this, their year﴾ is the year in which the proclamation of disavowal from the polytheists took place, which is the ninth year after the Hijrah.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾. ʿAylah means poverty; it is said: ʿala al-rajulu ya'ilu ʿaylatan if he became poor. The meaning: if you fear poverty because of the prevention by the disbelievers, ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. In this there are two issues:

The first issue: They mentioned several interpretations of this bounty:

First: Muqatil said: the people of Jeddah, San'a and Hunayn embraced Islam, and they brought food to Makkah, and Allah sufficed them the need to deal with the disbelievers.

Second: al-Hasan said: Allah made what is collected of the jizyah a substitute for that. It was also said: He enriched them with fay'.

Third: ʿIkrimah said: Allah sent down rain upon them, and their good increased.

The second issue: His saying ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ is a definite report about an unseen future matter concerning a great event, and the matter occurred in accordance with that report, so it was a miracle.

Then He said: ﴿if He wills﴾. Someone may ask: the purpose of this report is to remove fear of poverty, and this condition prevents achieving this aim. The answer comes in several ways:

First: that reliance on the attainment of this goal should not arise, so that a person is always humbly turning to Allah in seeking good and warding off calamities.

Second: the purpose of mentioning this condition is to teach observing courtesy (adab), as in His saying: ﴿You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security﴾ [Al-Fath: 27].

Third: the purpose is to alert that the attainment of this meaning does not occur at all times and in all matters; because Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said in his supplication: ﴿and provide for its people of the fruits﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126], and the particle min indicates partiality, so His saying in this verse ﴿if He wills﴾ means that partiality.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: Knowing of your conditions, and Wise, who does not give or withhold except for wisdom and rightness. And Allah knows best.

**The Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 9, Verse 29 (Part 1 of 2)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they give the jizyah (poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Muslim rule) willingly while they are humbled.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the ruling concerning the polytheists in declaring disavowal of their covenant, and in declaring disavowal of them in themselves, and in the obligation to fight them, and in keeping them away from al-Masjid al-Haram, and He raised the objections they had raised and answered them with sound answers, He mentioned after this the ruling concerning the People of the Book, which is that they are to be fought until they give the jizyah. At that point they are allowed to remain upon what they are upon, subject to conditions, and they become at that time among the Ahl al-Dhimmah (protected non-Muslims) and those with a covenant. In the verse there are issues:

**The first issue:** Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned that the People of the Book, if they are described by four attributes, it becomes obligatory to fight them until they become Muslim, or until they give the jizyah.

The first attribute: they do not believe in Allah. Know that the people say, "We believe in Allah." However, the verification is that most of the Jews are Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists), and the Mushabbih claims that there is no existent except the body and what subsists in it. As for the existent that is neither a body nor subsisting in a body, he denies it. What has been established by proofs is that God exists and is neither a body nor subsisting in a body. Then the Mushabbih is a denier of the existence of God. Thus it is established that the Jews deny the existence of God.

If it is said: The Jews are of two kinds: among them are the Mushabbihah, and among them are the Muwahhidah (unitarians), just as the Muslims are likewise. Suppose that the Mushabbihah among them deny the existence of God; then what is your position regarding the Muwahhidah among the Jews?
