We say: Those do not fall under this verse. However, the imposition of the jizyah upon them is by saying: since the obligation of the jizyah has been established upon some of them, it is necessary to say it applies to all of them, by necessity, since there is no one who distinguishes between them.

As for the Christians: they say, "the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit," and incarnation (hulul) and union (ittihad), and all of that contradicts divinity.

If it is said: The sum of the discussion is that whoever disputes about one of the attributes of Allah is a denier of the existence of Allah, exalted is He. In that case it follows that you must say that most of the theologians (mutakallimun) are deniers of the existence of Allah, exalted is He, because most of them differ concerning the attributes of Allah, exalted is He.

Do you not see that the Ahl al-Sunnah differed with great severity in this domain? Al-Ash'ari affirmed subsistence (al-baqa') as an attribute, while al-Qadi denied it. Abd Allah ibn Sa'id affirmed eternity (al-qidam) as an attribute, while the rest denied it. Al-Qadi affirmed the perception of tastes, the perception of smells, and the perception of heat and cold, which are what in the case of humans are called the perception of smell, taste and touch. Ustadh Abu Ishaq denied it. Al-Qadi affirmed seven states (ahwal) for the seven attributes, caused by those attributes, and the deniers of states denied it. Abd Allah ibn Sa'id claimed that the speech of Allah in pre-eternity was neither a command, nor a prohibition, nor a report; then it became that in the sending down. The rest denied it. A group of the early companions affirmed for Allah five words: in command, prohibition, report, interrogation, and calling.

[Page 24]

The well-known position is that the speech of Allah, exalted is He, is one. They differed over whether the opposite of what is known is within the scope of power (maqdur) or not. Thus it is established by this that differences have arisen among our companions concerning the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, in these many respects. As for the differences of the Mu'tazilah and the rest of the sects concerning the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, they are too numerous to be mentioned in one place.

Once this is established, we say: Either the difference concerning the attributes necessitates denial of the essence, or it does not necessitate that. If it necessitates it, then it follows that most sects of the Muslims must be said to have denied God. If it does not necessitate it, then it does not follow from the position of some Jews, and the position of the Christians toward incarnation and union, that they are deniers of belief in Allah. Furthermore, the doctrine of the Christians is that the hypostasis of the Word (uqnum al-kalimah) indwelt in Jesus. The Hashwiyyah among the Muslims say: whoever recites the speech of Allah, the one who recites it is the very speech of Allah, exalted is He. The speech of Allah, though it is an attribute of Allah, enters the tongue of this reciter and the tongues of all reciters. When the speech of Allah is written on a body, the speech of Allah, exalted is He, has indwelt that body. The Christians only affirmed incarnation and union with respect to Jesus, whereas these fools affirmed the Word of Allah in every person who recites the Qur'an, and in every body on which the Qur'an is written. If it is valid regarding the Christians that they do not believe in Allah for this reason, then it must be valid regarding these Hururiyyah and Hulûliyyah that they do not believe in Allah. This is the articulation of this objection.

The answer: The proof indicates that whoever says that the God is a body is a denier of God, exalted is He. That is because the God of the world exists and is neither a body nor subsisting in a body. When the anthropomorphist denies this existent, he has denied the very essence of God, exalted is He. Thus the disagreement between the anthropomorphist and the unitarian is not about an attribute, but about the essence. So it is valid of the anthropomorphist that he does not believe in Allah. As for the issues you have recounted, they are disagreements concerning attributes, and so the difference is clear. As for imposing the doctrine of the Hulûliyyah and the Hururiyyah, we definitively declare them to be unbelievers. Allah, exalted is He, declared the Christians to be unbelievers because they believed in the indwelling of the Word "(Allah)" in Jesus, and these believed in the indwelling of the Word "(Allah)" in the tongues of all who recite the Qur'an, and in all the bodies on which the Qur'an is written. If the claim of indwelling regarding a single essence necessitates declaring unbelief, then the claim of indwelling regarding all persons and bodies necessitates declaring unbelief all the more.

The second attribute among their attributes is that they do not believe in the Last Day.

Know that what is reported of the Jews and the Christians is the denial of the bodily resurrection (al-ba'th al-jismani). It seems that they incline toward a spiritual resurrection (al-ba'th al-ruhani).

Know that we have explained in this book the kinds of spiritual felicities and miseries, and we have argued for the soundness of the position regarding them, and clarified the indication of many verses upon them. Nevertheless, we also affirm bodily felicities and miseries, and we acknowledge that Allah makes the people of Paradise such that they eat and drink, and enjoy themselves with maidens. There is no doubt that whoever denies the gathering (al-hashr) and the bodily resurrection has denied the explicit text of the Qur'an. Since the Jews and the Christians deny this meaning, it is established that they are deniers of the Last Day.

The third attribute among their attributes is His saying: ﴿and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾, and concerning it there are two aspects:

The first: they do not forbid what has been forbidden in the Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Messenger.

The second: Abu Rawq said: they do not act upon what is in the Torah and the Gospel; rather, they distorted both and brought many rulings from their own selves.

[Page 25]

The fourth attribute: His saying: ﴿and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book﴾. It is said: "So-and-so adopts (yadin) such-and-such," when he takes it as a religion, so it is his belief. So His saying "and who do not adopt the religion of truth" means: they do not believe in the validity of the religion of Islam, which is the religion of truth. When He, exalted is He, mentioned these four attributes, He said: ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾. By this He clarified that what is meant by those described by these four attributes are those who are among the People of the Book, and the purpose is to distinguish them from the polytheists in the ruling, because what is obligatory regarding the polytheists is fighting or Islam, and what is obligatory regarding the People of the Book is fighting, or Islam, or the jizyah.

\* \* \*

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾, and concerning it there are issues:

**The first issue:** Al-Wahidi said: the jizyah is what the mu'ahad (one under a covenant) gives for his covenant, and it is a form (fi'lah) from "jaza, yajzi," when he discharges what is upon him. They differed concerning His saying: ﴿willingly (ʿan yadin)﴾. The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying ﴿ʿan yadin﴾ either means the hand of the giver or the hand of the taker. If what is meant is the giver, then there are two aspects:

One of them: that what is meant by ﴿ʿan yadin﴾ is "compliant, not refusing," because whoever refuses and resists does not give his hand, unlike the obedient and submissive. For this reason it is said: "he gave his hand" when he submitted and obeyed. Do you not see the saying: "he pulled his hand from obedience," just as one says: "he removed the noose of obedience from his neck."

The second: that what is meant is "until they give it from hand to hand, in cash, not deferred, and not sent through the hand of someone, but from the hand of the giver to the hand of the taker."

As for when what is meant is the hand of the taker, then there are likewise two aspects:

The first: that what is meant is "until they give the jizyah from a hand that is overpowering and dominant over them for the Muslims," just as you say: "the hand in this matter belongs to so-and-so."

The second: that what is meant is "by way of a favor upon them," because accepting the jizyah from them and leaving their lives to them is a great blessing.

\* \* \*

As for His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾, the meaning is that the jizyah is taken from them with humiliation, abasement, and disgrace, by his bringing it himself on foot, not riding, and delivering it while he is standing and the one receiving it is seated, and he is seized by his beard, and it is said to him: "Pay the jizyah," even if he is paying it, and he is pushed on the back of his neck. This is the meaning of humiliation. It was also said: the meaning of humiliation here is the very act of giving the jizyah. The jurists have many rulings that follow from abasement and humiliation, which are mentioned in the books of jurisprudence.

\* \* \*

**The second issue:** concerning some of the rulings of this verse.

**The first ruling**

I have argued by this verse that a Muslim is not to be killed for a dhimmi. The manner of establishing it is that His saying ﴿fight them﴾ requires the obligation of fighting them, and that includes permission to kill them, and the non-obligation of qisas (retaliatory justice) because of killing them. So when He said ﴿until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾, we know that the sum of these rulings ends at the giving of the jizyah. For the whole to end, it suffices that one of its parts ceases. When the obligation to kill them and the permissibility of their blood is lifted, that whole has ceased, and there is no need, for the whole to cease, for all its parts to cease.

Once this is established, we say: His saying "fight a group of the People of the Book" indicates the non-obligation of qisas for killing them, and His saying ﴿until they give the jizyah﴾ does not necessitate the removal of that ruling, because the cessation of one of its parts, namely the obligation to kill them, is sufficient for the cessation of the whole. Therefore it is necessary that after paying the jizyah the non-obligation of qisas remains as it was.

\* \* \*

[Page 26]

**The second ruling**

The disbelievers are of two groups. One group is the worshippers of idols and the worshippers of what they have deemed good. These are not allowed to remain upon their religion by the taking of the jizyah, and it is obligatory to fight them until they say, "There is no god but Allah." The other group are the People of the Book, namely the Jews, the Christians, the Samaritans, and the Sabians. These two categories, their course regarding the People of the Book is the course regarding the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) among us. The Magians likewise, their course is the course of the People of the Book, because of his peace be upon him saying: "Treat them as you treat the People of the Book." It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) took the jizyah from the Magians of Hajar. So these must be fought until they give the jizyah and covenant with the Muslims to pay the jizyah.

We have said that the jizyah is taken only from the People of the Book, because when He, exalted is He, mentioned the four attributes, which is His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾, He restricted them to being among the People of the Book, which is His saying ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾. Applying that ruling to others would necessitate nullifying this explicitly stated restriction, and that is not permissible.

\* \* \*

Ruling three: On the amount of the jizya (poll tax). Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) imposed one dinar on every adult male. ʿUmar imposed on the poor among the dhimmis twelve dirhams, on those of middling means twenty-four, and on the wealthy forty-eight. Our companions (the Shafiʿis) said: The least of the jizya is one dinar, and nothing may be added to the dinar except by mutual consent. If they agree and undertake the increase, we impose two dinars on the middling and four dinars on the rich. The evidence for what we have mentioned is that the original position is the prohibition of taking the property of a responsible person, except that His saying ﴿until they pay the jizya﴾ indicates that something is to be taken. What we have stated is the minimum amount, so it is permissible to take it, while the excess over it is not indicated by the word jizya, and the original position regarding it is prohibition, so it must remain upon that.
* * *
Ruling four: According to Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) the jizya is collected at the beginning of the year, and according to al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him) at its end.

Ruling five: According to Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) the jizya falls away by conversion to Islam and by death, due to his saying (peace be upon him): "There is no jizya upon a Muslim." According to al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him) it does not fall away.

Ruling six: Our companions said: These people were only permitted to remain upon their false religion by the taking of the jizya, out of respect for their forefathers who died upon the truth of the Torah and the Gospel law. Also, we allowed them to keep their possessions, so perhaps they will reflect and recognize the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his prophethood. Therefore they were given respite for this reason. And Allah knows best.
* * *
Two questions remain here:

The first question: Ibn al-Rawandi used to attack the Qur'an and say: It mentioned, in magnifying the disbelief of the Christians, His saying: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains fall down in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ ﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful that He should take a son﴾ [Maryam: 90–92]. So it clarified that their declaration of this statement reached this degree. Then, when He took from them one dinar, He left them upon it and did not prevent them from it.
The answer: The purpose of taking the jizya is not to confirm him in disbelief, but rather its purpose is to preserve his blood and to give him respite for a period, in hope that during this period he may come to understand the excellences of Islam and the strength of its proofs, and so pass from disbelief to faith.

The second question: Is paying the jizya alone sufficient to preserve blood, or not?
The answer: It is necessary, together with it, to inflict humiliation and abasement upon the disbeliever, and the reason is that the nature of a rational person recoils from bearing humiliation and abasement. So when the disbeliever is given respite for a period while he observes the might of Islam, hears the proofs of its soundness, and sees the humiliation and abasement in disbelief, it is apparent that this will move him to transfer to Islam. This is the purpose of prescribing the jizya.

**Al-Razi's commentary (*Mafatih al-Ghayb*) on Surah 9, verse 30:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Jews say, "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths. They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾

Within the verse there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that when the Exalted, in the preceding verse, judged the Jews and Christians to be people who do not believe in Allah, He explained this in this verse. He reported that they affirmed a son for Allah. Whoever permits this regarding the Divine is, in reality, a denier of God. He also made clear that they are on the same level as the polytheists in associating partners with Allah, even though the ways of asserting partnership differ. There is no difference between one who worships an idol and one who worships the Messiah or anything else, because shirk means nothing other than a person taking an object of worship alongside Allah. Once this meaning is realized, shirk has occurred. Indeed, if we reflect, we will know that the disbelief of the idol-worshipper is lighter than the disbelief of the Christians. The idol-worshipper does not say that this idol is the creator and god of the world; rather, he treats it as something through which he seeks nearness to Allah's obedience. The Christians, however, affirm incarnation (*hulul*) and union (*ittihad*), and that is an extremely ugly disbelief. Thus it is established that there is no difference between these incarnationists and the rest of the polytheists. Allah specified their acceptance of the jizya (poll tax) from them only because, outwardly, they attached themselves to Musa and ʿIsa and claimed that they act in accordance with the Torah and the Gospel. Because of the veneration of these two exalted messengers, the veneration of their scriptures, and the veneration of the forebears of these Jews and Christians, who were upon the true religion, Allah the Exalted decreed the acceptance of the jizya from them. Otherwise, in reality, there is no difference between them and the polytheists.

**The second issue:** Regarding His saying: ﴿The Jews say, "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah"﴾, there are several views.

The first: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: This statement was made only by one man among the Jews, named Finhas ibn ʿAzurāʾ.

The second: Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima, said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely Sallam ibn Mishkam, al-Nuʿman ibn Awfa, and Malik ibn al-Sayf, and they said: "How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah?" Then this verse was revealed. According to these two views, those who hold this doctrine are some of the Jews. However, Allah attributed that statement to the Jews as a whole, in accordance with the Arabic custom of applying the name of a group to one individual. It is said: "So-and-so rides horses," though he may have ridden only one of them; and "So-and-so keeps company with the rulers," though he may keep company with only one of them.

The third view: Perhaps this doctrine was widespread among them and then died out, and Allah reported it about them. The denial of the Jews of this is of no consequence, for Allah's report about them is more truthful. The reason for which they said this statement is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated: the Jews neglected the Torah and acted contrary to the truth, so Allah the Exalted caused them to forget the Torah and erased it from their hearts. ʿUzayr then humbled himself before Allah and entreated Him, and the memory of the Torah returned to his heart. He then warned his people with it. When they tested him, they found him truthful in it, and they said: "This was made easy for ʿUzayr only because he is the son of Allah." Al-Kalbi said: Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) killed their scholars, so no one remained among them who knew the Torah. Al-Suddi said: The ʿAmaliqa (Amalekites) killed them, so no one remained among them who knew the Torah. This is what has been said on this subject.

As for Allah's report about the Christians, that they say "The Messiah is the son of Allah," it is clear. However, there is a strong difficulty with it. We are certain that the Messiah, may Allah's blessings be upon him, and his companions were free from calling people to anything except the paternity and filiation, for this is the most vile type of disbelief. How, then, is it fitting for the great prophets, peace be upon them? If that is the case, how is it conceivable that the entire body of the lovers of ʿIsa among the Christians agreed upon this disbelief? And who originated this corrupt doctrine, and how was he able to attribute it to the Messiah, peace be upon him? The commentators answered this question by saying: The followers of ʿIsa, peace and blessings be upon him, remained upon the truth after the raising of ʿIsa, until a war occurred between them and the Jews. Among the Jews there was a courageous man called Bulus (Paul), who killed a group of the companions of ʿIsa. Then he said to the Jews: "If the truth is with ʿIsa, then we have disbelieved, and the Fire is our destination. We would be losers if they enter Paradise and we enter the Fire. I will devise a plan and mislead them." So he hamstrung his horse and displayed remorse for what he had been doing. He placed dust upon his head and said: "I was called from the heavens: there is no repentance for you except that you become a Christian." He had repented. So the Christians admitted him into the church, and he remained for a year without going out, and he studied the Gospel. They believed him and loved him. Then he went to Bayt al-Maqdis, and he appointed over them a man named Nastur, and taught him that ʿIsa, Maryam and God were three. He then went to the Romans and taught them *lahut* (divinity) and *nasut* (humanity), saying: "ʿIsa was not a human being, nor a body, but he was God." He taught this also to another man called Yaʿqub. Then he summoned a man called Malka and said to him: "God has never ceased to be, and ʿIsa will never cease to be." Then he prayed for these three, and said to each one of them: "You are my successor; call the people to your Gospel. I have seen ʿIsa in a dream, and he is pleased with me, and I am sacrificing myself to gain the pleasure of ʿIsa." Then he entered the altar and slaughtered himself. Then each of these three called the people to his statement and doctrine. This is the cause of the occurrence of this disbelief among the sects of the Christians. This is what al-Wahidi, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, related.

The closer view to me is that it may be said: Perhaps the word "son" occurred in the Gospel as an honorific, just as the word "khalil" (friend) occurred concerning Ibrahim as an honorific. Then these people, out of enmity toward the Jews, and in order to counter their corrupt excess in one extreme with a corrupt excess in the other extreme, exaggerated and interpreted the word "son" as literal filiation. The ignorant accepted this, and this corrupt doctrine spread among the followers of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. Allah knows the reality of the matter best.

**The third issue:** ʿAsim, al-Kisaʾi and ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read ﴿ʿUzayr﴾ with tanwin (nunation: the final "n" sound), while the rest read it without tanwin. Al-Zajjaj said: The correct reading is with tanwin. So ﴿ʿUzayr﴾ is the *mubtadaʾ* (subject of the nominal sentence), and ﴿the son of Allah﴾ is its *khabar* (predicate). If this is the case, tanwin is necessary in the state of ease, because ʿUzayr is declinable, whether it is non-Arabic or Arabic. The reason for its being declinable is two things:

The first: It is a light noun, so it is declinable, even though it is non-Arabic, like Hud and Lut.

The second: It is in the diminutive form (*taṣghir*), and non-Arabic names are not made diminutive.

As for those who omitted the tanwin, they have three possible explanations:

The first possibility: It is non-Arabic and definite, so it must be indeclinable.

The second possibility: The word "ibn" is an attribute (*sifa*), and the predicate is omitted. The estimate is: "ʿUzayr, the son of Allah, is our object of worship." ʿAbd al-Qahir al-Jurjani criticised this possibility in his book *Dala'il al-I'jaz*, saying: When a noun is described with an attribute and then a predicate is given about it, whoever denies it directs the denial to the predicate, and that attribute becomes accepted. Since the intended object of denial is their saying "ʿUzayr, the son of Allah, is our object of worship," the denial would be directed at his being an object of worship for them, and his being the son of Allah would be established; and it is known that this is disbelief. In my view, this criticism is weak. As for his statement that whoever reports about a described entity a matter and someone denies it, the denial is directed at the predicate, this is accepted. But as for his statement that this would be an acceptance of that attribute, this is disputed, because it does not follow from one's denying that predicate that it indicates that everything else does not deny it, rather that it affirms it. This is based on *dalil al-khitab* (implication drawn from the wording), which is weak, especially in a context like this.

The third possibility: Al-Farraʾ said: The nunation's "n" is silent in ﴿ʿUzayr﴾, and the "b" in His saying ﴿ibn Allah﴾ is also silent, so two silent letters meet here, and the nunation "n" is deleted for ease. Al-Farraʾ cited:

*"So I left him, not one who seeks to please, nor one who remembers Allah except a little."*

Know that when He related this report about them, He said: ﴿That is their statement from their mouths﴾.

One may ask: Every statement is uttered from the mouth, so what is the meaning of specifying this statement with this description?

The answer has several aspects:

The first: It means a statement not supported by any proof; it is merely a phrase they utter, empty of any meaning that merits consideration. The sum is that they spoke a statement with their tongues, but no effect of that statement was produced in the intellect, because attributing offspring to God, who is exalted above need, desire, lying with, and intercourse, is a false statement, and the intellect has no effect from it. A similar example is His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾.

The second: A person may choose a doctrine either by way of allusion or by way of symbol and indirect expression. When he states it explicitly and mentions it with his tongue, that is the utmost in his choosing that doctrine and the ultimate in his being one who adheres to it and speaks by it. What is meant here is that they declare this doctrine openly and do not conceal it at all.

The third: What is meant is that they called people to this statement until this statement came to be on the mouths and tongues, and what is meant by it is their exaggeration in calling people to the doctrine.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾. On this there are several issues.

**The first issue:** There are several interpretations of this verse.

The first: What is meant is that this statement by the Jews and Christians resembles the statement of the polytheists: "The angels are the daughters of Allah."

The second: The pronoun refers to the Christians, meaning: their saying "The Messiah is the son of Allah" resembles the saying of the Jews "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah," because they (the Jews) are older than them.

The third: This statement of the Christians resembles the statement of their predecessors, meaning that it is an ancient disbelief, so it is not a newly invented one.

**The second issue:** *Al-muḍahāh* means likeness (*al-mushābaha*). Al-Farraʾ said: It is said "ḍāhaytuhu" (I resembled him), "ḍahiyyan," and "muḍāhāh," and this is the statement of most lexicographers regarding *muḍāhāh*. Shimr said: *Al-muḍāhāh* means following: it is said "so-and-so yuḍāhī so-and-so," meaning he follows him.

**The third issue:** ʿAsim read ﴿yuḍāhi'ūn﴾ with a hamza and with a kasra on the "h," while the rest read it without a hamza and with a damma on the "h." It is said: "ḍāhaytuhu" and "ḍāha'tuhu" are two dialectal forms, like "arjaytu" and "arja'tu." Aḥmad ibn Yahya said: No one followed ʿAsim in the hamza.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾ That is: they deserve to be told this statement, in amazement at the vileness of their statement, as one says: "The people rode a lion; may Allah destroy them, how wondrous is their act!" ﴿How are they deluded?﴾ *Al-ifk* means turning away. It is said: "Afika al-rajulu ʿan al-khayr," meaning he was turned and diverted, and "rajulun ma'fuk" means a man turned away from goodness.

So His saying ﴿how are they deluded?﴾ means: how are they diverted and turned away from the truth after the proof has become clear, until they make a son for Allah! This amazement is only directed at the creation, and Allah the Exalted is not amazed at anything, but this address is in accordance with the Arabs' custom in their discourse. Allah the Exalted made His Prophet marvel at their abandonment of the truth and their persistence in falsehood.

The Exalted said: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no god but He. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, described the Jews and the Christians with another kind of associationism (shirk), in His words: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾

In this verse there are several issues.

**The first issue:** Abu 'Ubayda said: the *ahbar* (rabbis, sing. *habr* or *hibr*) are the jurists (*fuqaha'*). The scholars differed concerning its singular form. Some say *habr*, others say *hibr*. Al-Asma'i said: "I do not know whether it is *al-habr* or *al-hibr*." Abu al-Haytham used to say: the singular of *al-ahbar* is *habr* with a fatha only, and he rejected the kasra. Al-Layth and Ibn al-Sikkit used to say: *habr* and *hibr* are both used for a scholar, whether he is a dhimmi or a Muslim, provided he is from the People of the Book. The People of Meanings (*Ahl al-Ma'ani*) said: the *habr* is the scholar who, by his craft, adorns (*yuhabbir*) meanings and expresses them well. The *rahib* (monk) is one in whom fear and reverence (*al-khashya*) have taken firm root in his heart, and the traces of reverence appear on his face and in his clothing. In common usage, *al-ahbar* came to refer specifically to the scholars of the Jews from the descendants of Harun (Aaron), and *al-ruhban* to the scholars of the Christians, the people of the monasteries (*al-sawami'*).

**The second issue:** Most of the exegetes said: the meaning of "lords" (*arbab*) is not that they believed these men to be the gods of the worlds. Rather, the meaning is that they obeyed them in their commands and prohibitions. It is reported that 'Adi ibn Hatim was a Christian, and he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was reciting Surat Bara'a, and he reached this verse. He said: I said, "We do not worship them." He (ﷺ) said: "Do they not forbid what Allah has permitted so that you forbid it, and make lawful what Allah has forbidden so that you deem it lawful?" I said, "Yes." He said: "That is their worship."

Al-Rabi' said: I said to Abu al-'Aliyah: "How was that lordship (*rububiyya*) among the Children of Israel?" He said: "They would sometimes find in the Book of Allah something that contradicted the sayings of the rabbis and the monks, so they would take up the sayings of these men, and they would not accept the ruling of the Book of Allah, the Exalted."

[Page 31]

Our teacher and master, the seal of the verifiers and the independent jurists, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I have witnessed a group of those who follow the jurists blindly (*muqallidat al-fuqaha'*). I read to them many verses of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, on some issues, while their schools of law were contrary to those verses. They did not accept those verses, nor did they pay them any attention. They remained looking at me as one in wonder, meaning: how is it possible to act upon the apparent meanings of these verses when the transmitted reports from our predecessors came in opposition to them? If you reflect carefully, you will find this disease spreading through the veins of most of the people of this world.

If it is said: He, the Exalted, declared them disbelievers because they obeyed the rabbis and the monks. Therefore the sinner who obeys Satan should be ruled a disbeliever, as is the position of the Khawarij (a sect that declared grave sinners to be disbelievers).

The answer: the sinner, although he accepts the call of Satan, does not revere him. Rather, he curses him and treats him with contempt. As for those followers, they accepted the sayings of the rabbis and the monks and revered them. Thus the difference is clear.

The second opinion concerning the interpretation of this lordship is that the ignorant and the Hashwiyya (a term for the uneducated literalists), when they exaggerate in revering their shaykh and their exemplar, their natures may incline toward the belief in indwelling (*hulul*, the divine dwelling in a human being) and union (*ittihad*, the merging of the divine with the human). If that shaykh seeks worldly gain and is far from religion, he may suggest to them that the matter is as they say and believe. I have witnessed some deceivers, far removed from religion, who used to order their followers and companions to prostrate to him, and he would say to them: "You are my slaves." He would tell them things about indwelling and union, and if he were alone with some of the foolish among his followers, he might claim divinity. If this occurs among this community, how is it unlikely that it occurred among the earlier nations?

The sum of the discussion is that this lordship may mean either that they obeyed them in matters where they opposed the command of Allah, or that they accepted kinds of disbelief and so disbelieved in Allah, and this became like taking them as lords besides Allah, or that they attributed to them indwelling and union. All these four aspects are witnessed and found in this community.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Yet they were commanded only to worship one God﴾. Its meaning is clear: the Torah, the Gospel and the divine books all declare this.

Then He said: ﴿There is no god but He. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.﴾ That is: He is exalted above having a partner in command and obligation, above having a partner in being prostrated to and worshipped, and above having a partner in deserving the utmost glorification and reverence.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 32:

﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

Know that the purpose of this verse is to explain a third kind of the evil deeds that proceeded from the leaders of the Jews and the Christians. It is their striving to nullify the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ), and their diligence in concealing the proofs that indicate the truth of his law and the strength of his religion. By "the light" is meant the proofs that indicate the truth of his prophethood, and these are very many:

The first of them: the overpowering miracles (mu'jizat) that appeared at his hand. The miracle either is a proof of truthfulness or it is not. If it is a proof of truthfulness, then wherever a miracle appears there must be truthfulness, so it is necessary that Muhammad (ﷺ) is truthful. If it does not indicate truthfulness, then this would cast doubt on the prophethood of Musa and Isa, peace be upon them both.

The second: the Great Qur'an, which appeared on the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ), although from the beginning of his life to its end he had not learned, nor studied, nor acquired knowledge, nor looked into a book. This is among the greatest of miracles.

The third: the essence of his law is the glorification of Allah and praise of Him, submission to His obedience, turning the soul away from love of this world, and encouragement toward the happiness of the Hereafter. Reason indicates that there is no path to Allah except through this way.

The fourth: his law was free of all defects. There is in it no attribution of what does not befit Allah, and no call to other than Allah. He possessed great lands, yet he did not change his way of despising this world and disregarding it. Had his aim been the pursuit of worldly gain, the matter would not have remained so. These circumstances are clear proofs and overpowering demonstrations of the soundness of his claim. Then they, with their feeble words, their flimsy doubts, and their various kinds of scheming and deceit, sought to nullify these proofs. This is like one who wishes to extinguish the light of the sun by blowing on it. Just as that is futile and a lost effort, so is this. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾. Then He, exalted is He, promised Muhammad (ﷺ) increased victory, strength, elevation of rank, and perfection of station, saying: ﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

If it is said: How is it permissible to say "Allah refuses except such-and-such," when one does not say "I dislike or hate except Zayd"?

We reply: The word (abā) is treated as (lam yurid), "did not will," and the meaning is: Allah did not will anything but that. However, refusal (ibā') conveys an added degree of non-willing, which is prevention and refusal. The evidence for this is his (ﷺ) saying: "If they intend to wrong us, we refuse," for which he was praised. It is not permissible to praise someone for merely disliking wrongdoing, because that is possible for both the strong and the weak. One says: "So-and-so refuses oppression (abā al-ḍaym)." The meaning is what we have mentioned. The proofs were called "light" only because light guides to what is right, and in the same way proofs guide to what is right in religions.

[Page 32]

He, it is who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it. [Qur'an 9:33]

Know that when He, exalted is He, related about the enemies that they were trying to nullify the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ), and explained that He refuses that nullification and that He will complete His affair, He then explained the manner of that completion, saying: ﴿He it is who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾.

Know that the perfection of the state of the Prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them, is attained only through a combination of matters. The first of them: the abundance of proofs and miracles, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿has sent His Messenger with guidance﴾.

The second: that His religion includes matters whose rightness, soundness, conformity with wisdom, and agreement with benefit in this world and the Hereafter are evident to everyone, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and the religion of truth﴾.

The third: that His religion becomes dominant over all other religions, prevailing over them, overpowering their adherents and subduing those who deny it, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾.

Know that the prevalence of one thing over another may be by argument, may be by numbers and abundance, and may be by victory and dominance. It is known that He, exalted is He, gave glad tidings of this, and it is not permissible that glad tidings be given except of a matter that is future and not yet existing. The prevalence of this religion by argument is already established and known, so it is necessary to interpret it as prevalence by victory.

If it is said: the apparent meaning of His saying ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ requires that it be dominant over all religions, and the matter is not so, for Islam did not become dominant over all other religions in the land of India, China, Rum, and the rest of the lands of the disbelievers.

We say: they answered this objection in several ways:

The first way: there is no religion other than Islam except that the Muslims have overpowered it and prevailed over it in some places, even if not in all its places. They overpowered the Jews and expelled them from the lands of the Arabs, they overcame the Christians in the lands of al-Sham and what adjoins it toward the direction of Rum and the West, they overcame the Magians in their kingdom, and they overcame the idol-worshippers in many of their lands bordering the Turks and India. Likewise with all other religions. Thus it is established that what Allah reported in this verse has occurred and come to pass, and that this was a report of the unseen, and therefore it is a miracle.

The second way in the answer: we say, it is reported from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "This is a promise from Allah that He, exalted is He, will make Islam high above all religions, and the complete fulfilment of this occurs at the descent of Isa." al-Suddi said: "That occurs at the emergence of the Mahdi, and no one will remain except that he enters Islam or pays the kharaj (land tax)."

The third way: the meaning is: that He may make Islam prevail over every religion in the Arabian Peninsula (Jazirat al-Arab), and this has been achieved, for He, exalted is He, did not leave in it any of the disbelievers.

The fourth way: that the meaning of His saying ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ is that He will make him (the Messenger) acquainted with all the laws of the religion, and inform him of them entirely, so that nothing of them remains hidden from him.

The fifth way: that the meaning of His saying ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ is by argument and clarification. However, this is weak, because this is a promise that He, exalted is He, will do it, while the strengthening by argument and clarification was already present from the beginning of the affair. It may be answered that at the beginning of the affair the doubts were numerous because of the weakness of the believers and the domination of the disbelievers, and the disbelievers prevented the rest of people from reflecting upon those proofs. But after the strength of the state of Islam, the disbelievers were rendered powerless and the doubts weakened, so the manifestness of the proofs of Islam became stronger. Thus the intended meaning of that glad tiding was this increase.

[Page 33]

[Page 34]

The Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people by falsehood and bar [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day when it is heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides and their backs are branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾

Know that when He, the Exalted, described the leaders of the Jews and the Christians with arrogance, tyranny, the claim of lordship, and exaltation over creation, He described them in this verse with greed and eagerness to take people's wealth. This is to alert us that the purpose of displaying that lordship, tyranny and boasting is taking people's wealth by falsehood. By my life, whoever reflects on the condition of the people of religious authority and forgery in our time will find that these verses seem to have been revealed only concerning them and to describe their condition. You see one of them claiming that he does not turn to this world, that his heart is not attached to any of the creatures, and that he is in purity and sinlessness like the nearest angels. But when the matter comes down to a single loaf of bread, you see him fawning over it, and enduring the utmost humiliation and baseness in obtaining it.

There are several issues concerning the verse:

**The first issue:** You have learned that the *ahbar* (rabbis) are from among the Jews and the *ruhban* (monks) from among the Christians, according to common usage. Allah, the Exalted, relates of many of them that they devour people's wealth by falsehood. On this there are discussions:

**The first discussion:** He, the Exalted, restricted this by saying ﴿many﴾, to indicate that this practice belongs to some of them, not to all of them. For the world is never free of truth, and the consensus of all of them upon falsehood is practically impossible. This may give the impression that just as the consensus of this Ummah upon falsehood does not occur, the same holds for all other nations.

**The second discussion:** He, the Exalted, expressed the taking of wealth with the word "eating," which is His saying ﴿they devour﴾. The reason for this metaphor is that the greatest aim of gathering wealth is eating, so the thing is named after its greatest purpose. Or it may be said: whoever eats something has taken it into himself and prevented it from reaching others, and whoever gathers wealth has added that wealth to himself and prevented it from reaching others. Since there is a resemblance between eating and taking in this respect, taking was called eating. Or it may be said: whoever takes people's wealth, when he is asked to return it, says, "I ate it and it is no longer here, so I cannot return it." For this reason, taking was called eating.

**The third discussion:** He said ﴿devour the wealth of people by falsehood﴾, and the scholars have differed on the interpretation of this "falsehood" in several ways:

First: They used to take bribes in return for lightening rulings and being lenient in the laws.

Second: They used to claim, before the common people and the ignorant among them, that no one could attain the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, except through serving and obeying them and spending wealth seeking their approval. The common people were deceived by these lies.

Third: The Torah contained verses indicating the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). Those rabbis and monks would offer corrupt interpretations of them and carry them to false meanings, and they would comfort the hearts of their common followers with this, and take bribes.

Fourth: They would establish among their common followers that the true religion is the one they follow. Once they had established this, they would say: strengthening the true religion is obligatory; and then they would say: there is no way to strengthen it except when those jurists are great people possessing much wealth and great accumulations. By this means they would lead the common people to spend themselves and their wealth in serving them. This is the falsehood by which they devoured people's wealth, and all of it is present in our time. It is the path by which most of the ignorant and the forgers take the wealth of the common people and the foolish of creation.

﴿And they bar [them] from the way of Allah﴾, because they would kill [people] for following them, and prevent [people] from following the righteous of creation and the scholars of the age. In the time of Muhammad, upon him be prayers and peace, they would exert great effort in preventing [people] from following him by every kind of deception and trickery.

The author, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The ultimate aim of created beings in this world is wealth and status. In describing the rabbis and monks, the Exalted explained that they were passionately devoted to these two things. Wealth is what is meant by His saying ﴿they devour the wealth of people by falsehood﴾, and status is what is meant by His saying ﴿and they bar [them] from the way of Allah﴾. For if they acknowledged that Muhammad was upon the truth, following him would become obligatory for them, and then their rule would collapse and their sanctity would vanish. Out of fear of this harm, they exerted themselves in preventing people from following Muhammad (ﷺ), in casting doubts, in devising means of trickery and deceit, and in preventing people from accepting his true religion and following his sound way.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

There are issues in the verse:

**The first issue:** Concerning His saying ﴿those who﴾, there are three possibilities. It may be that what is meant by "those who" is those rabbis and monks. It may be that it is a new statement, as some have said: what is meant is those Muslims who withhold zakat (obligatory almsgiving). It may be that what is meant is everyone who hoards wealth and does not pay out of it the obligatory rights, whether he is one of the rabbis and monks or one of the Muslims. There is no doubt that the wording admits each of these three meanings. It is narrated from Zayd ibn Wahb that he said: I passed by Abu Dharr and said, "O Abu Dharr, what brought you to this land?" He said: "I was in Syria and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾." Mu'awiyah said: "This verse was revealed concerning the People of the Book." I said: "It concerns them and us." This became a cause of estrangement between me and him. Then Uthman wrote to me asking me to come to him. When I arrived at Medina, the people turned away from me as though they had never seen me before. I complained of this to Uthman, and he said to me: "Withdraw a little from [here]. By Allah, I will not abandon what I used to say." It is also narrated from al-Ahnaf that he said: When I arrived at Medina I saw Abu Dharr saying: "Give the disbelievers tidings of a hot stone heated in the fire of Hell, which is placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out from the shoulder-blade of his back, until his body dissolves, and it is placed on the shoulder-blade until it comes out from the nipple." When the people heard this they left him. I followed him and said: "I did not see these people except that they disliked what you said to them." He said: "What can Quraysh do to me?"

Our master, may Allah be pleased with him, said: If what is intended is to restrict this threat to those previously mentioned, namely the People of the Book, then the meaning is that He described them with intense greed for taking people's wealth by His saying ﴿they devour the wealth of people by falsehood﴾, and He also described them with intense miserliness and refusal to pay the obligatory dues from their own wealth by His saying ﴿and those who hoard gold and silver﴾. If what is intended is the Muslims who withhold zakat, then the meaning is that He described the ugliness of their way in greed for taking people's wealth by falsehood, then He urged the Muslims to pay the obligatory rights from their wealth and explained the severe threat for abandoning it. If what is intended is everyone, then the meaning is that He described them with greed for taking people's wealth by falsehood, and then followed it with a threat for everyone who refrains from paying the obligatory rights from his wealth, as an alert that since the condition of one who withholds his own wealth wrongfully is such, then what do you think of the condition of one who strives to take another's wealth by falsehood, forgery and trickery?

* * *

**The second issue:** The root meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the speech of the Arabs is gathering. Anything whose parts are gathered together is called *maknuz* (hoarded). It is said: "This is a body with compact parts (*muktaniz al-ajza'*)" when its parts are assembled together. The scholars of the Companions differed about what is meant by this blameworthy hoarding. Most of them said: it is wealth whose zakat has not been paid. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "What you have paid its zakat on is not hoarding." Ibn ʿUmar said: "Whatever you have paid its zakat on is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths; and whatever you have not paid its zakat on is hoarding, even if it is above the earth." Jabir said: "If you remove the charity from that [wealth], you have removed its evil from it, and it is not hoarding." Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾, said: "He means those who do not pay the zakat of their wealth." The Qadi said: Restricting this meaning to withholding zakat has no basis. Rather, the correct statement is that hoarding is wealth from which what must be paid has not been paid. There is no difference between zakat and what is obligatory of expiations (*kaffarat*), what is required for the expenses of the pilgrimage or Friday prayer, what must be paid in debts and rights, spending on family or dependents, compensation for damages, and blood-money for injuries. So in all these categories, it must be included in the threat.

The second view: When a large amount of wealth is gathered, it is the blameworthy hoarding, whether its zakat has been paid or not. Those who held the first view supported their position with several matters:

First: the generality of His saying ﴿It gains what it has earned﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:286], for this indicates that whatever a person has acquired is his right. Likewise His saying ﴿He does not ask you for your wealth﴾ [Muhammad 47:36], and His saying, upon him be prayers and peace: "What an excellent wealth for a righteous man." And His saying, peace be upon him: "Every person has more right to his own earnings." And His saying, peace be upon him: "What has had its zakat paid is not hoarding, even if it is underground; and what has reached the point of requiring zakat and has not had it paid is hoarding, even if it is above ground."

Second: In the time of the Messenger, peace be upon him, there was a group such as Uthman and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, and he, peace be upon him, counted them among the great believers.

Third: He, peace be upon him, urged giving a third or less [of one's wealth as charity] during illness. If gathering wealth were forbidden, he, peace be upon him, would have approved of the sick person giving away all of it in charity; rather, he would have commanded the healthy person to do so during his health.

Those who held the second view argued with several points:

First: the generality of this verse. There is no doubt that its apparent meaning is evidence for the prohibition of gathering wealth. So to hold that gathering is permissible after paying zakat is to abandon the apparent meaning of this verse, and one should not turn to that except with a separate proof.

Second: What Salim ibn al-Ja'd narrated: when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. They said to him: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" He said: "A tongue that remembers [Allah], a humble heart, and a wife who helps one of you in his religion." He, peace be upon him, also said: "Whoever leaves behind gold or silver will be branded with it." A man died and a dinar was found in his loincloth; he, peace be upon him, said: "A brand." Another died and two dinars were found in his loincloth; he, peace be upon him, said: "Two brands."

Third: What is narrated from the Companions on this matter. ʿAli said: "Every wealth exceeding four thousand [dirhams] is hoarding, whether you have paid zakat from it or not." It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah: "Every gold or silver that its owner has tied up (*awka*) is hoarding." It is narrated from Abu al-Darda': whenever he saw a caravan bringing wealth, he would climb onto a high place and say: "The caravan has come bearing fire," and "Give the hoarders tidings of branding on the foreheads, sides, backs and bellies."

[Page 37]

The fourth: God, exalted is He, created wealth only so that it could be used as a means of meeting needs. When a person has obtained the amount with which he can meet his need, and then gathers wealth beyond that, he gains no benefit from the excess, because it exceeds his need. He also withholds it from others who could meet their need with it. So this person, by this withholding, becomes a barrier to the manifestation of His wisdom and a barrier to the arrival of God's kindness to His servants.

Know that the correct position is to say: it is preferable that a man seeking religion (*al-tālib li-l-dīn*) not gather much wealth. However, he is not forbidden from it according to the apparent *sharī'a* (the sacred law). The first is understood as a matter of piety (*taqwā*), and the second as a matter of the apparent ruling (*fatwā*). As for demonstrating that it is preferable to avoid seeking much wealth, this is shown by several considerations.

The first consideration: when a person loves something, the more he attains it and the more he enjoys possessing it, the stronger his love for it becomes and the more intense his inclination. A poor person has, as it were, not tasted the pleasure of benefiting from wealth, and is as if he were unaware of that pleasure. When he possesses a little wealth, he finds pleasure in proportion to it, so his inclination grows stronger. Thus, the more his wealth increases, the more he enjoys it, and the more intense his greed in seeking it and his inclination to acquire it. It is established, then, that increasing wealth is a cause of increasing greed in seeking. Greed is exhausting to the spirit, the soul, and the heart, and its harm is severe. Therefore, it is incumbent upon the intelligent person to guard himself against harming his soul. Furthermore, we have shown that the more wealth there is, the greater the greed. Suppose the pursuit of wealth were to end at a limit beyond which the seeking stops and greed disappears; then a person would strive to reach that limit. But since it has been proven by evidence that the more wealth one owns, the greater the harm arising from greed, and that this harm and this seeking have no end, it is incumbent upon a person to abandon it at the outset, as the poet said:

*He saw the matter leads to another, so its end becomes its beginning.*

The second consideration: earning wealth is extremely difficult, and preserving it after it has been acquired is even more burdensome, harder, and more arduous. So a person spends his whole life, at one time in pursuit of acquisition and at another in the toil of preservation. Then he benefits from it only a little, and eventually leaves it behind with regrets and sighs. That is the manifest loss.

The third consideration: abundance of wealth and status produces arrogance, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6–7]. Arrogance prevents the servant from reaching the station of the good pleasure of the Most Merciful, and brings him to loss and abandonment.

The fourth consideration: God, exalted is He, prescribed *zakāt* (obligatory almsgiving), and that is an effort to diminish wealth. If increasing wealth were a virtue, the sacred law would not strive to diminish it.

If it is asked: why did he, peace be upon him, say: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand"?

We answer: the upper hand only gives him the attribute of being better, because he gave that little. Because a small deficiency occurred in his wealth, the quality of being better was obtained by him; and because the poor man received that small increase, the quality of being inferior was obtained.

* * *

The third issue: many reports have come concerning the threat against those who withhold *zakāt*. As for withholding the *zakāt* on money, it is His saying in this verse: ﴿On the day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾. As for withholding the *zakāt* on livestock, it is what has been related in a hadith: that God punishes the owners of livestock who do not pay its *zakāt* by driving those animals toward Him in their largest bodily form. They trample their owners with their hooves and gore them with their horns. Whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them returns to them, and it continues thus until people are finished with the reckoning.

* * *

The fourth issue: the correct position in our view is that *zakāt* is obligatory on ornaments (*ḥilī*). The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God – give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾.

If it is said: this threat applies only to men, not to women.

We answer: we are speaking of a man who acquired ornaments for his wives. Furthermore, the ordering of this threat upon the accumulation of gold and silver is a judgment ordered upon a descriptive attribute that is suitable to it, namely that accumulating this wealth prevents one from spending it on the needy, even though there is no need for it. For if he needed to spend it, he would not have been able to accumulate it. And the action of a non-needy person in withholding wealth from the needy is suitable for him to be prevented from doing so. Thus it is established that this threat is ordered upon a suitable attribute, and a ruling mentioned following a suitable attribute must be understood as being caused by it. Therefore, this threat is for that accumulation, and wherever that attribute occurs, that threat must accompany it.

Furthermore, the general texts that enjoin *zakāt* apply to permissible ornaments. He, peace be upon him, said: "Bring the quarter of a tenth of your wealth." He said: "On silver (*al-riqqa*) the quarter of a tenth is due." He said: "O 'Ali, you owe *zakāt*. When you possess twenty *mithqāl*, give half a *mithqāl*." He said: "There is no right in wealth beyond *zakāt*." He said: "There is no *zakāt* on wealth until a year has passed over it." So this verse, together with all these reports, makes *zakāt* obligatory on permissible ornaments.

Then we say: no contrary evidence to this proof has been found in the Book, and this is clear, because there is nothing in the Qur'an indicating that there is *zakāt* on permissible ornaments. Nor has any contrary evidence been found in the reports, except that our companions (the Shāfi'īs) have cited a report: his saying, peace be upon him: "There is no *zakāt* on permissible ornaments." However, Abū 'Īsā al-Tirmidhī said: no sound report has come from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concerning ornaments. Furthermore, even if this report were sound, we would interpret it as referring to pearls, because he said: "There is no *zakāt* on ornaments," and the word *ḥilī* is singular and defined by the article *al-*. We have shown that if there is a prior known referent, the word must be understood in reference to it, and the known referent for the word *ḥilī* in the Qur'an is pearls. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and you extract from it ornaments that you wear﴾ [al-Naḥl: 14]. Since this is the case, the word *ḥilī* is understood to refer to pearls, and so its evidential force falls away. Also, caution favours the position that *zakāt* is obligatory. Moreover, it is not possible to oppose this explicit text with analogy (*qiyās*), because explicit text is superior to analogy. Thus it is established that the truth is what we have stated.

* * *

The fifth issue: God, exalted is He, mentioned two things, namely gold and silver. Then He said: ﴿and do not spend them﴾, and regarding this there are two views.

The first: the pronoun refers to the meaning, in several ways.

One of them: each of the two is a category, and that which is hoarded is dinars and dirhams. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 9].

The second: the implied meaning is "and do not spend the hoards."

The third: al-Zajjāj said: the implied meaning is "and do not spend those possessions."

The second view: the pronoun refers to the wording, and in this there are several possibilities.

One of them: the implied meaning is "and do not spend the silver," and gold is omitted, because it is included within silver in that both share the quality of being prices for things, both are noble substances, and both are intended for hoarding. Since the two share most of their attributes, mentioning one suffices instead of mentioning the other.

The second: mentioning one may suffice in place of the other, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see a trade or amusement, they scatter toward it﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11], where the pronoun is taken to refer to trade. And He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or a transgression and then throws it upon an innocent person﴾ [al-Nisā': 112], where the pronoun refers to the sin.

The third: the implied meaning is "and do not spend them, and the gold likewise," just as the meaning of his saying is: *"And I and Qayyār are strangers in it,"* that is: "and Qayyār likewise."

If it is asked: what is the reason that these two were singled out for mention from among all other wealth?

We answer: because they are the principal valued forms of wealth, and they are the ones intended for hoarding.

Know that when God, exalted is He, mentioned those who hoard gold and silver, He said: ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. That is, inform them in the manner of mockery (*tahakkum*), because those who hoard gold and silver do so in order to use them as a means to obtain relief on the day of need. So it was said: this is the relief, just as one says: their greeting is nothing but beating, and their honouring is nothing but insult. Furthermore, "tidings" (*bishāra*) refers to good news that affects the heart, so that the colour of the face's complexion changes because of it. This includes a case where the complexion changes because of joy or because of sorrow.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day when it will be heated up in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it. "This is what you hoarded for yourselves."﴾ In the reading of Ubayy (وبُطُونُهم, "and their bellies") instead of "their backs." And there are questions concerning it:

The first question: It is not said "aḥmaytu ʿalā al-ḥadīd" (I heated upon the iron); rather it is said "aḥmaytu al-ḥadīd" (I heated the iron). So what is the purpose of His saying: ﴿on the Day when it will be heated up upon them﴾?

The answer: The meaning is not that those wealths are heated over the fire, but rather that the fire is heated upon those wealths, which are gold and silver. That is, a fire of intense heat and burning is kindled upon them. This is derived from His saying: ﴿a blazing fire﴾ (nārun ḥāmiyah). Had it been said "on the Day when they are heated," this benefit would not have been conveyed.

If they say: Since the intended meaning is "on the Day when the fire is heated upon them," why was the verb mentioned [in the form it is]?

We say: Because the feminine gender of "fire" (nār) is merely grammatical (lafẓī), and the verb is not, in its apparent form, attributed to it, but rather to the phrase ﴿upon them﴾. Therefore both the masculine and the feminine forms are acceptable. It is also reported from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read (tuḥmā) with a ta' (feminine prefix).

The second question: What governs the word ﴿Day﴾ (yawma)?

The answer: The implied sense is: "So give them the good news of a painful punishment on the Day when it will be heated up upon them."

The third question: Why were these particular limbs singled out?

The answer comes in several respects:

The first: The purpose of acquiring wealth is the attainment of joy in the heart, the effect of which appears in the face; the attainment of satiety, by which the sides swell; and wearing luxurious garments, which they drape over their backs. Since they sought the adornment of these three limbs, the branding indeed fell upon the foreheads, the sides and the backs.

The second: These three limbs are hollow, and within them are delicate organs which suffer intensely from the arrival of even the slightest effect upon them, unlike the rest of the limbs.

The third: Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: These places were singled out for mention because when the owner of wealth sees a poor man beside him, he withdraws from him and turns his back.

The fourth: The meaning is that they will be branded on the four directions: from the front, upon the forehead; from behind, upon the backs; and from the right and left, upon the two sides.

The fifth: The most delicate parts of a human being are his forehead, the intermediate part in delicacy and firmness is his side, and the part that is hardest of a human's limbs is his back. So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that these three categories of his limbs will be submerged in the branding, and the purpose of this is to draw attention to the fact that that branding occurs upon those limbs.

The sixth: The perfection of a human body lies in its beauty and its strength. As for beauty, its seat is the face, and the most precious of the limbs of the face is the forehead; so when branding falls upon the forehead, beauty has entirely vanished. As for strength, its seat is the back and the sides; so when branding falls upon them, strength has departed from the body. The conclusion: the occurrence of branding upon these three limbs necessitates the loss of beauty and the loss of strength, and a human seeks wealth only to attain beauty and to attain strength.

The fourth question: Is it all of that wealth that becomes a brand upon the human body, or only the obligatory portion of zakat?

The answer: The apparent requirement of the verse is the whole; for since it has not been paid out, the right [owed] from it is not a specific portion, but rather no part of it exists without the right being attached to it. Therefore Allah must punish him with all of its parts.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves.﴾ The implied sense is: "It will be said to them: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste [it]." The purpose of this is to magnify the threat, for when they witness what they are punished with, whether a dirham, a dinar, or a plate made of them or of one of them, they would suppose it might be the right that they withheld, and they would suppose otherwise. So Allah magnifies their rebuke by saying to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves; you did not prefer with it the pleasure of your Lord, nor did you intend by spending from it the benefit of your own selves and your deliverance by it from the punishment of your Lord. So you became as though you had stored it up so that it would be made a punishment for you, on account of what you are now witnessing." Then Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾, meaning: you did not spend it on the benefits of your religion and your worldly life in accordance with what Allah commanded you, ﴿so taste﴾ the consequence of that, because of it and not because of anything else.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 36 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein. And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾

Know that this is an explanation of the third category of the abominable deeds of the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists, namely their undertaking to strive to change the rulings of Allah. This is because He, the Exalted, decrees a specific ruling for each period, and when they changed those rulings through the nasi' (intercalation), that became an effort on their part to alter the ruling of the sunnah according to their desires and opinions, and this was an increase in their disbelief and their regret. There are several issues in the verse.

The first issue: Know that the sanah (year) among the Arabs refers to twelve months of the lunar months, and the evidence for this is this verse. Also, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the calculation﴾ [Yunus: 5]. So He made the measuring of the moon by its phases the cause of the years and the calculation, and this is only valid if the year is tied to the course of the moon. Also, the Exalted said: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: they are measures of time for the people and for the Hajj﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189]. And among all other groups, the year is a reference to the period in which the sun completes one full revolution. The lunar year is shorter than the solar year by a known amount, and because of that deficiency the lunar months shift from one season to another, so the Hajj would fall in winter at one time and in summer at another, and the matter would be hardship for them because of this. Also, when they attended the Hajj they attended for trade, so that time might not coincide with the arrival of merchants from distant regions, and this would disrupt their trade. For this reason they undertook the practice of the kabisah (intercalary adjustment), as is known in the science of astronomical tables (zij), and they took the solar year as the reference. At that point the time of the Hajj remained fixed to one specific time suited to their interests, and they benefited from their trade and their affairs. So this nasi', although it was a cause for obtaining worldly benefits, nevertheless entailed a change in the ruling of Allah the Exalted, because when He specified the Hajj to particular months by definite designation, that nasi' caused a change in the ruling and obligation of Allah in the other months.

The summary: for the sake of safeguarding their worldly interests, they strove to change the rulings of Allah and to nullify His obligations, and for this reason they deserved the great censure in this verse.

Know that since the solar year exceeds the lunar year, they gathered that excess, and when its amount reached a month, they made that year thirteen months. Allah the Exalted rejected this from them and said: indeed the ruling of Allah is that the year be twelve months, neither less nor more. Their arbitrary determination concerning some years, that it becomes thirteen months, is a ruling that stands contrary to the ruling of Allah the Exalted and necessitates changing the obligations of Allah the Exalted, and all of that is contrary to the religion.

Know that the doctrine of the Arabs from the earliest times was that the year should be lunar, not solar, and this was a ruling they inherited from Ibrahim and Isma'il, upon them be the blessings and peace. As for the Jews and the Christians, it was not so. Then some of the Arabs learned the manner of the kabisah from the Jews and the Christians, and they made this apparent in the lands of the Arabs.

The second issue: Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: it is not permissible for the phrase ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ to be connected to the phrase ﴿the number of months﴾, because that would require separating the relative clause from the relative pronoun by the predicate, which is the phrase ﴿twelve months﴾, and that is not permissible. I say: there are several possibilities in the grammatical analysis of this verse:

The first: we say that the phrase ﴿the number of months﴾ is the subject (mubtada') and the phrase ﴿twelve months﴾ is the predicate (khabar). The phrases ﴿with Allah﴾, ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, and ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾ are adverbial phrases of time and place, some of which are substituted (badal) for others, and the meaning is: indeed the number of months, twelve months, with Allah, in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth. The purpose of mentioning these successive substitutions is to establish that this number is necessary and fixed in the knowledge of Allah, and in the Book of Allah from the very first moment Allah the Exalted created the world.

The second: the saying of the Exalted ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ is connected to an omitted element that serves as an attribute of the predicate. Its meaning is: twelve months established in the Book of Allah. Then it is not permissible for this Book to mean a book among the books, because it is connected to the saying ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth, of them four are sacred﴾, and names of concrete entities do not connect to adverbs of time; you do not say "your servant on Friday." Rather, the Book here is a verbal noun (masdar), and the meaning is: indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, that is, in His ruling that took effect the day He created the heavens.

The third: that the Book is a noun. The phrase ﴿the day He created the heavens﴾ is connected to an omitted verb, and the meaning is: indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months written in the Book of Allah, which He wrote the day He created the heavens and the earth.

The third issue: concerning the explanation of the rulings of the verse: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah﴾, that is, in His knowledge, ﴿twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾. Regarding the explanation of "the Book of Allah" there are several views:

The first: Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which He recorded the states of all His creatures in detail, and it is the source of the books that Allah sent down to all the prophets, upon them be peace.

The second: some said: what is meant by the Book is the Qur'an, and we have mentioned verses that indicate that the year that is considered in the religion of Muhammad ﷺ is the lunar year, and if that is so, this ruling is written in the Qur'an.

The third: Abu Muslim said: ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ means: in what He has obligated and decreed, and the Book in this place is the ruling and the obligation, like His saying: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216], ﴿Retaliation has been prescribed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178], ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 54]. The judge (al-Qadi) said: this view is distant, because He, the Exalted, placed the Book in this verse as a container, and if the Book is taken to mean the reckoning, that would not hold except by way of metaphor. It may be answered: although it is a metaphor, it is a commonly used metaphor, as one says: the matter is such and such in the reckoning of so-and-so and in his ruling.

As for the saying ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾, we have mentioned in the second issue several possibilities regarding what it is connected to, and the closest is what we mentioned in the third possibility, namely that the meaning is that He wrote this ruling and decreed it the day He created the heavens and the earth. The purpose is to show that this ruling was decreed from the very beginning of the creation of the world, and this indicates emphasis and affirmation.

* * *

As for the saying ﴿of them four are sacred﴾: they unanimously agreed that these four are, of them, three consecutive (sard): Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and one single (fard), which is Rajab. The meaning of "sacred" (hurum) is that disobedience in them incurs a more severe punishment, and obedience in them yields greater reward. The Arabs used to exalt them greatly, to the extent that if a man met the killer of his father, he would not touch him.

If it is said: the parts of time are alike in reality, so what is the cause of this distinction?

We say: this meaning is not improbable in the sacred laws, for its examples are many.
