Do you not see that He distinguished the Sacred City from the rest of the lands with greater sanctity, and distinguished Friday from the rest of the days of the week with greater sanctity, and distinguished the Day of 'Arafah from other days by that particular worship, and distinguished the month of Ramadan from the other months with greater sanctity, which is the obligation of fasting, and distinguished some hours of the day by the obligation of prayer in them, and distinguished some nights from the rest, which is the Night of Power, and distinguished some persons from the rest of people by bestowing the robe of prophethood? If these examples are apparent and well known, then what is improbable about singling out some months with greater sanctity? Then we say: it is not improbable that Allah the Exalted knows that performing obedience in these times has a greater effect on the purification of the soul, and committing sins in them has a stronger effect on the corruption of the soul, and this is not improbable according to the wise. Do you not see that among them are those who wrote books on the times in which supplications are hoped to be answered, and they mentioned that those specific times have causes that make this so. "The Prophet ﷺ was asked: which fasting is best? He ﷺ said: 'The best of it after the fasting of Ramadan is the fasting of the month of Allah, al-Muharram.'" And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever fasts one day of the sacred months of Allah, for him there are thirty days' reward for each day." And many jurists made the blood money (diyah) heavier upon the killer because the killing occurred in these months. There is another benefit in this: human natures are inclined to injustice and corruption, and refraining from these abominations absolutely is difficult for them. So Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, singled out some times for greater veneration and respect, and singled out some places for greater veneration and respect, so that a person may refrain, in those times and in those places, from abominations and evil deeds. This yields kinds of virtues and benefits:

First: that abandoning those abominations in those times is something required, because it reduces abominations.

Second: that when he abandons them in those times, his abandoning them at those times may become a cause for his inclination of nature to turn away from them entirely.

Third: that when a person performs acts of obedience in those times and turns away from sins in them, then after those times pass, if he begins to commit abominations and sins, his beginning them becomes a cause for nullifying what he endured of hardship and difficulty in performing those acts of obedience in those times, and the apparent state of the sensible person is that he would not be content with that, so this becomes a cause for his avoiding sins altogether. This is the wisdom in singling out some times and some places for greater veneration and respect.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, and in it there are two discussions:

The first discussion: the phrase ﴿that﴾ refers either to the saying ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾, neither more nor less, or to the saying ﴿of them four are sacred﴾. My view is that the first is preferable, because the disbelievers conceded that four of them are sacred, but because of the kabisah they sometimes made the year thirteen months and changed the positions of the months, and the purpose of this verse is to refute these people, so the wording must be taken to refer to that.

The second discussion: regarding the explanation of the word "religion" (din) there are several views:

The first: the word din may be intended to mean reckoning, as it is said: "The shrewd person is the one who calls himself to account" (dana nafsahu), meaning he reckons it. The qayyim means the straight. So the interpretation of the verse on this basis is: that is the straight, correct reckoning and the perfect justice.

The second: al-Hasan said: that is the upright religion that is not altered and not changed. The qayyim here means the standing one that is not altered and not changed, the enduring one that does not cease, and it is the religion upon which people were created (fitrah).

The third view is that the intended meaning is that this worship (ta'abbud) is the binding religion in Islam. The judge (al-Qadi) said: Taking the word "religion" (din) to mean worship is no better than taking it to mean reckoning (hisab), because the latter is its metaphorical sense. It can be argued that the root meaning of the word din is submission (inqiyad). One says, "O you to whom necks have submitted (dānat lahu al-riqab)," meaning they yielded. Reckoning is therefore called din because it necessitates submission, and the waiting period ('iddah) is also called din. So there is no reason to prefer taking this word to mean worship over taking it to mean reckoning. The scholars said: By the ruling of this verse, Muslims are obliged to rely on the Arabic lunar year, reckoned by the crescent moons (ahilla), in their sales, the terms of their debts, the due dates of their zakat, and all their other rulings. It is not permissible for them to rely on the non-Arab (ajami) or Roman solar year.

* * *

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾. There are two discussions regarding this:

First discussion: Regarding the pronoun in His words ﴿therein﴾, there are two views.

The first, which is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, is that the meaning is: "Do not wrong yourselves in the twelve months." The purpose is to prohibit a person from embarking on corruption at all times throughout his life.

The second, which is the view of the majority, is that the pronoun in His words ﴿therein﴾ refers to the four sacred months (al-hurum, the months in which fighting is forbidden). They said: The reason for this is what we have mentioned, that certain times have an effect in increasing the reward for acts of obedience and the punishment for forbidden acts. The evidence that this view is preferable consists of several points:

The first: The pronoun in His words ﴿therein﴾ refers to the previously mentioned noun, so it must refer to the nearest of the mentioned nouns, and that is none other than His words ﴿of them four are sacred﴾.

The second: God the Exalted singled out these months with additional sanctity in another verse, His words: ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months, so whoever undertakes the Hajj therein, there shall be no sexual intercourse, no wickedness, and no disputing during the Hajj﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:197]. These things are also impermissible outside the Hajj, but God emphasized the prohibition of them in these days to draw attention to their increased nobility.

The third: Al-Farra' said: The preferable view is that the pronoun refers to the four months, because the Arabs say ﴿therein﴾ for numbers between three and ten, and when the number exceeds this, they say ﴿feminine﴾ (fiha). The principle here is that the plural of paucity (jam' qillah) is referred to with a pronoun as one would refer to a feminine plural group, and the plural of abundance (jam' kathrah) is referred to as one would refer to a single feminine noun. As Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"For us are the bright dishes that shine in the forenoon,
and our swords drip blood from battle."

He said "yalma'na" (they shine) and "yaqturna" (they drip) because "al-asyaf" (the swords) and "al-jafanat" (the dishes) are plurals of paucity. Had he used the plural of abundance, he would have said "talma'" and "taqtur." This is the preferred usage. Then it is permissible to treat one of the two plurals as the other, as in the words of al-Nabigha:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords
have notches from the clashing of battalions."

He said "bihinna" (with them, feminine plural) even though "al-suyuf" (the swords) is a plural of abundance.

Second discussion: Regarding the interpretation of this wronging, there are several views:

The first: It means the intercalation (al-nasi') that they used to practice, by which they would shift the Hajj from the month in which God commanded it to be performed to another month, and would alter God the Exalted's obligations.

The second: That He forbade fighting in these months.

The third: That He forbade all acts of disobedience, for the reason we have mentioned, that these months have a special effect in magnifying reward and punishment. The view closest to me is to interpret it as a prohibition of intercalation (nasi'), because God the Exalted mentioned it immediately after the verse.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together, as they fight you all together﴾. There are several discussions regarding this:

First discussion: Al-Farra' said: ﴿all together﴾ means collectively. The word kaffah does not take a masculine form, nor is it made plural according to the number of men, so one does not say "kaffin" or "kaffat" for women. Rather it is ﴿kaffah﴾ with the feminine ending and in the singular, because although it has the form of the active participle (fa'ilah), it functions as a verbal noun, like khassah and 'ammah. That is why the Arabs did not add the definite article (al-) to it, since it follows the pattern of your saying "they stood together (ma'an)" and "they stood all together (jami'an)." Al-Zajjaj said: "Kaffah" is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and it may not be made dual or plural, just as when you say "fight them in general (‘ammah)," you do not make it dual or plural, and likewise "khassah" (specifically).

Second discussion: Regarding His words ﴿kaffah﴾ there are two views:

The first: That the meaning is "fight them with all of you, united in fighting them," just as they fight you in this manner. The meaning is: cooperate and support one another in this, do not abandon one another, do not sever ties, and be the servants of God united and agreeing in fighting the enemies.

The second: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Fight them with your entire strength, and do not show favour to some of them by refraining from fighting, just as they consider it lawful to fight all of you." The first view is closer, so that one side may be compared with the other.

Third discussion: The apparent meaning of His words ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ is the permission to fight them in all the months. Some people say: Fighting the disbelievers is forbidden, based on His words: ﴿Of them four are sacred; that is the upright religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, meaning: do not wrong yourselves therein by making fighting and raiding lawful during them. We have already discussed this question in Surat al-Baqarah in explaining His words: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:217].

[p. 45]

Then He said: ﴿And know that God is with those who are mindful of Him﴾, meaning: with His allies who fear Him in performing acts of obedience and in avoiding what is forbidden. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is that He guarantees them victory.

﴿The postponement (al-nasi') is only an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and forbidden another year, to conform to the number of what God has forbidden, so that they make lawful what God has forbidden. The evil of their deeds is made attractive to them, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 37:

﴿Indeed, the postponing (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and forbidden another year, to match the number of what Allah has forbidden, so that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Among the issues concerning the verse:

**The first issue:** Regarding *al-nasi'* (postponement, the intercalation practice), there are two opinions.

**The first opinion:** It means postponement. Abu Zayd said: "I made the camels wait (*nasa'tu al-ibil*) away from the watering-trough, *an사u-hā nas'an*, when I delayed them. *Anse'tuhu inса'an* means I delayed him from it. The noun is *al-nasi'ah* and *al-nas'*." From this comes "Allah postponed (*ansa'a*) the term of so-and-so," and "he delayed (*nasa'a*) in his term." Abu Ali al-Farisi said: *al-nasiyy* is a verbal noun, like *al-nadhir* and *al-nakir*. It is also possible that *nasi'* means *mansu'* (postponed), as *qatil* means *maqtul* (killed). However, it is not possible that the intended meaning here is the passive, because if it were understood that way, the meaning would be: "The postponed item is only an increase in disbelief," and the postponed item would be the month. That would make the month itself disbelief, which is false. Rather, the intended meaning of *al-nasi'* here is the verbal noun in the sense of *al-ins'* (postponing), which is delay. In the case of months, *al-nasi'* was an expression for postponing the sanctity of one month to another month that does not possess that sanctity. It is narrated from Ibn Kathir through the route of Shibl that *al-nas'* (with the vowel pattern of *al-naf'*) is the true verbal noun, as in their saying *nasa'tu*, meaning "I postponed." It is also narrated from him: *al-nasiyy* with the *ya'* lightened, which is probably a dialect form of *al-nasi'* with the hamza, like *arjaytu* and *arja'tu*. It is also narrated from him: *al-nasiyy* with the *ya'* doubled and without a hamza, and this is a regular easing.

**The second opinion:** Qutrub said: *al-nasi'* originally derives from increase. It is said: *nasa'a fi al-ajal* and *ansa'a* when he added to the term. Likewise milk is called *al-nas'* because water is added to it. A woman *nasa'at* when she became pregnant, as he considered the increase of the child within her to be like the increase of water in milk. It is also said of a she-camel: *nasa'tuha*, meaning I drove her so that her pace would increase. Every increase that occurs in a thing is *nasi'*.

Al-Wahidi said: The correct view is the first opinion, namely that the root meaning of *al-nasi'* is postponement. A woman *nasa'at* when she became pregnant, because her menses were delayed. *Nasa'tu al-naqah* means I delayed her relative to others, so that the mixing of some of them with others would not prevent a good march. *Nasa'tu al-laban* means I delayed it until much water had entered it.

Having understood these two opinions, we say: The people knew that if they ordered their reckoning according to the lunar year, their pilgrimage would fall at one time in summer and at another time in winter, and their journeys would be difficult for them. They would not benefit from them in trade and commerce, because the rest of the people from other lands did not come except at the suitable and appropriate times. So they knew that basing affairs on observing the lunar year harms the interests of this world, so they abandoned that and took the solar year as their reference. Since the solar year exceeds the lunar year by a fixed amount, they needed the intercalation (*kabisah*), and two matters resulted for them from that intercalation:

The first: They used to make some years thirteen months, because of the accumulation of those additions.

The second: The pilgrimage would shift from one lunar month to another. So in some years the pilgrimage would fall in Dhu al-Hijjah, and after that in Muharram, and after that in Safar, and so on in cycles, until after a specific period it returned once more to Dhu al-Hijjah. Thus two matters resulted from the intercalation:

The first: the increase in the number of months.

The second: the postponement of the sanctity belonging to one month to another month.

We have already shown that the word *al-nasi'* indicates postponement according to the majority, and indicates increase according to the rest. On both assessments, it applies to these two matters.

The conclusion from this discussion is: basing the acts of worship on the lunar year harms the interests of this world, while basing them on the solar year achieves the interests of this world. Allah, however, had commanded them, from the time of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), to base the matter on observing the lunar year. They abandoned Allah's command regarding observing the lunar year and took the solar year into account for the sake of worldly interests, and they placed the pilgrimage in a month other than the sacred months. For this reason Allah reproached them and made it a cause for the increase of their disbelief. It was a cause for the increase of disbelief because Allah had commanded them to perform the pilgrimage in the sacred months, and then, by means of this intercalation, they performed it in other than these months. They also told their followers that what they had done was the obligatory matter, and that performing it in the lunar months was not obligatory. So this was a rejection by them of Allah's ruling despite knowing it, and a rebellion against His obedience. That necessitates disbelief by the consensus (*ijma'*) of the Muslims. Thus it is established that their practice of that postponement necessitates an increase in disbelief. As for the calculation by which the amount of the increase resulting from those intercalations is known, it is mentioned in the astronomical tables (*zijat*).

As for the commentators (*mufassirun*), they mentioned another reason for this postponement. They said: The Arabs used to forbid four months, and this was an established law from the time of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both). The Arabs were people of wars and raids, and it was hard for them to remain for three consecutive months without raiding during them. They said: If three consecutive sacred months pass, we will not gain anything in them, and we will perish. So they would postpone the prohibition of Muharram to Safar, so they would forbid it and make lawful the sacred month (Muharram).

Al-Wahidi said: Most scholars hold that this postponement was not confined to one month, but occurred in all the months. This view, in our opinion, is the correct one according to what we have established. And they agreed that when he (peace be upon him) intended to perform the Hajj in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, the pilgrimage returned in reality to the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. So he (peace be upon him) said: "Verily, time has returned to the form it had on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months." He meant that the sacred months had returned to their proper places. (ﷺ)

* * *

**The second issue:** Allah's words ﴿an increase in disbelief﴾ mean: Allah related of them many kinds of disbelief. When they added this practice to those kinds mentioned previously, and we have shown that this practice is disbelief, the addition of this practice to those kinds mentioned earlier became an increase in disbelief. Al-Jubba'i used this verse as evidence against the view of those who say that faith is merely belief and affirmation. He said: Because Allah made clear that this practice is an increase in disbelief, and an increase over disbelief must be a completion, so abandoning this postponement was faith. It is evident that this abandoning is neither knowledge nor affirmation, so it is established that something other than knowledge and affirmation may be faith.

The author, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This argument is weak. For we have shown that when Allah made it obligatory upon them to perform the Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah, for example, according to the lunar months, if we consider the solar year, the Hajj may fall in Muharram at one time and in Safar at another. So their saying that this Hajj is valid and suffices, and that it is not obligatory upon them to perform the Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah, if it was from them by a ruling known necessarily to be from the religion of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), that was disbelief due to lack of knowledge and due to lack of affirmation.

As for Allah's words ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾ (*yudallu bihi alladhina kafaru*), this is the reading of the majority, and it is good, as the leading astray is ascribed to those who disbelieved. For if they were astray themselves, it is good to ascribe leading astray to them, and if they were leading others astray, it is also good, because one who leads others astray is necessarily astray himself. The reading of the people of Kufa is ﴿yudallu﴾ with the *ya'* vowelled with a *damma* and the *dad* with a *fatha*, and its meaning is: their great ones lead them astray by compelling them to this postponement of the months. So the verb is ascribed to the object, as in His saying in this verse: ﴿the evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾, meaning: those who compelled them to it made that attractive to them.

Abu Amr, in a narration through the route of Ibn Miqsam, read (*yudallu bihi alladhina kafaru*) with the *ya'* vowelled with a *damma* and the *dad* with a *kasra*. It has three possibilities:

The first: Allah leads astray by it those who disbelieve.

The second: Satan leads astray by it those who disbelieve.

The third, which is the strongest: it leads astray by it those who disbelieve, meaning their followers and those who take up their sayings. This possibility is the strongest because neither Allah nor Satan has been mentioned.

Know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿yudallu bihi﴾ refers to *al-nasi'*. And His saying ﴿they make it lawful one year and forbidden another year﴾: the pronoun refers to *al-nasi'*, and the meaning is: they make that postponement lawful one year and forbid it another year. Al-Wahidi said: They make the postponement lawful in the year in which they want to fight in Muharram, and they make the postponement forbidden in another year, which is the year in which they leave Muharram upon its prohibition. The author, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This interpretation is valid only if we interpret *al-nasi'* as meaning that they used to postpone Muharram in some years. That requires that the sacred month be turned into lawful and vice versa. However, this is only suitable if we take *al-nasi'* as the passive, namely the postponed item (*al-mansu'* al-mu'akhkhar), and we have mentioned that this is problematic, because it requires that the postponed month be disbelief, and that this is impermissible unless we say that what is meant by *al-nasi'* is the postponed item, which is the passive. We would then interpret His saying ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾ as meaning the practice by which the postponement becomes a cause of increase in disbelief. By means of this supposition, this interpretation becomes stronger.

As for His saying ﴿so that they may tally the number of what Allah has forbidden﴾ (*li-yuwati'u 'iddata ma harrama Allah*): the lexicographers said: one says *wati'tu fulanan 'ala kadha* when I agreed with him upon it. Al-Mubarrad said: one says *tawati'a al-qawm 'ala kadha* when they gathered upon it, each one stepping where his companion steps. The *iyta'* in poetry derives from this, which is that the poet brings two rhyming words in the same poem with one form and one meaning. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: They did not make lawful a month of the sacred months except that they forbade in its place a month of the lawful months, and they did not forbid a month of the lawful months except that they made lawful in its place a month of the sacred months, so that the number of the sacred months would be four, matching what Allah the Exalted had mentioned. This is what is meant by *muwata'ah* (agreement in number).

When the Exalted made clear that this practice was disbelief and reprehensible, He said: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: He means Satan made this practice attractive to them, and Allah does not guide every sinful disbeliever.
