Then He, exalted is He, concluded the verse with His words: ﴿And it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ On this there are two issues:

Issue 1: The purpose of this statement is to alert to their blame and to associate them with women, children, and the infirm, whose custom is sitting in their homes. They are the ones who sit back and the ones who remain behind (al-khalifun wa'l-khawalif), as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿They were content to be with those who remain behind﴾ [al-Tawbah: 87].

Issue 2: Scholars differed over who said this statement. It is possible that the speaker was Satan, by way of whispering (waswasah). It is possible that some of them said it to others when they wanted to gather together in staying behind, because whoever undertakes corruption loves to multiply its kinds. It is possible that the speaker was the Messenger (ﷺ) when he gave them permission to stay behind, and so Allah rebuked him. It is possible that the speaker was Allah, glorified is He, because He disliked their going out for corruption, and the meaning was: if you are corrupters, then Allah dislikes your setting out in this manner, so He commanded you to sit back from this particular going out.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verses 44–46 (part 1 of 2):

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their selves. God knows well the God-fearing.﴾ ﴿It is only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day, whose hearts are in doubt, who ask your permission. They are hesitating in their doubt.﴾ ﴿Had they wished to go out, they would have made ready some preparation for it. But God disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn 'Abbas said that His words ﴿do not ask your permission﴾ refer to the period after the expedition of Tabuk. The others said: this is not permissible, because what comes before this verse and what comes after it were revealed concerning the story of Tabuk, and the purpose of this discourse is to distinguish the believers from the hypocrites. For the believers, when they are commanded to go out to jihad, hasten to it and do not hesitate, whereas the hypocrites hesitate, become sluggish, and bring excuses and pretexts. This purpose is achieved whether it is expressed in the form of the present tense or the past tense. The point is that He, exalted is He, made asking for permission in that situation the sign of hypocrisy, and God knows best.

The second issue: His words ﴿those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive﴾ contain an elided element, and the implied meaning is "in respect of striving." However, the elision is acceptable because it is evident. Here there are two opinions:

The first opinion: this statement is to be taken at face value without any further implied element. On this reading, the meaning is that it is not the habit of believers to ask your permission to strive. The senior figures among the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar) used to say: "We do not ask the Prophet ﷺ for permission to fight, for our Lord has urged us to it again and again, so what is the benefit of asking permission?" They were such that if the Messenger had ordered them to stay behind, it would have been hard for them. Do you not see that when 'Ali ibn Abi Talib was ordered by the Messenger of God ﷺ to remain in Medina, it was hard for him, and he was not content until the Messenger said to him: "You stand to me in the same position as Harun stood to Musa"?

The second opinion: there must necessarily be another implied element here. They said: because leaving off seeking the permission of the Imam for jihad is not permissible, and God censured these people for leaving off this seeking of permission, it is established that an implied element is necessary. The sense is: "These people do not ask your permission not to strive." The negative particle has been omitted, and a parallel is His words: ﴿God makes clear to you so that you do not go astray﴾ [An-Nisa: 176]. What indicates this omitted element is that what comes before the verse and what comes after it shows that the censure arose specifically from asking permission to remain behind, and God knows best.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day, whose hearts are in doubt, who ask your permission. They are hesitating in their doubt.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: He clarified that this departure (from the duty of striving) does not happen except when there is no faith in God and the Last Day. Then, since the absence of faith may be caused by doubt about it, or may be caused by a firm and definite conviction of its absence, God, exalted is He, clarified that the absence of faith in these people was caused by doubt and uncertainty, and this indicates that the one who doubts and is uncertain is not a believer in God. Here there are two questions:

The first question: if knowledge is inferential (istidlali), then the occurrence of doubt about the evidence entails the occurrence of doubt about what the evidence establishes, and the occurrence of doubt about a single premise among the premises of an argument is sufficient for doubt about the soundness of the argument. This implies that a believer, whenever a question or difficulty occurs to him concerning one of the premises of his argument, would become doubtful about what is established by it, and this would imply that the believer leaves his faith at every moment, because a question or difficulty has come to his mind. It is known that this is false. Therefore it is established that the foundation of faith is not on argument but on taqlid (unquestioning acceptance of authority). Thus this verse indicates that the origin of faith is taqlid in this respect.

The answer: although the Muslim may be struck by doubt concerning the soundness of some premises of a single argument, all the other proofs remain free from criticism in his view. For this reason his faith always remains steady and continuous.

The second question: Do not your companions say, "We are believers, God willing"? That implies the occurrence of doubt.

The answer: We have thoroughly investigated this question in the commentary on His words in surah al-Anfal: ﴿Those are the true believers﴾ [Al-Anfal: 74].

The second issue: The Karramiyya said: faith is nothing but mere verbal affirmation, although He, exalted is He, testified against them in this verse that they are not believers.

The third issue: His words ﴿and their hearts are in doubt﴾ indicate that the locus of doubt is the heart alone. And when the locus of doubt is the heart, the locus of knowledge and faith is also the heart, because the locus of one of two opposites must be the locus of the other opposite. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those, He has inscribed faith in their hearts﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 22]. And when the locus of knowledge and disbelief is the heart, then in reality it is the heart that is rewarded or punished, and the other parts follow it.

The fourth issue: His words ﴿so they remain hesitating in their doubt﴾ mean that the doubter who is uncertain remains wavering between negation and affirmation, not judging for either of the two parts and not firmly committed to either of two contradictories. Its explanation: belief is either firm or not firm. If it is firm and does not correspond to reality, it is ignorance (jahl). If it corresponds to reality and is based on certainty, it is knowledge ('ilm); otherwise it is the belief of the one who practises taqlid. If it is not firm, then if one of the two sides is preponderant, the preponderant side is conjecture (zann) and the outweighed side is illusion (wahm). If the two sides are equal, it is doubt (rayb) and uncertainty (shakk), and in that case the person remains hesitating between the two sides.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Had they wished to go out, they would have made ready some preparation for it.﴾ It is read ''uddatahu'' (with a definite object), and it is also read ''iddatan'' with the vowel of the 'ayn being i, without an annexation and with an annexation. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means provisions, water, and a mount, because their journey was long and in a difficult season, and their not making ready preparation is evidence that they intended to stay behind. Others said: this is an indication that they were well-off and able to obtain the equipment and provisions.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But God disliked their setting out, so He held them back.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: al-inba'ath means setting out to do something. It is said: "I made the camel rise, and it rose"; "I sent it for such a matter, and it set out"; and "He dispatched him on such a matter," meaning he carried it out. And al-tathbit means turning a person back from the action he had resolved upon. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, disliked their going out with the Messenger ﷺ, so He turned them away from it.

If it is said: their going out with the Messenger must either be considered a corruption (mafsadah) or a benefit (maslahah). If we say it was a corruption, why did He rebuke the Messenger for permitting them to remain behind? And if we say it was a benefit, why did He say that He disliked their setting out and going out?

The correct answer: their going out with the Messenger was not a benefit, as is shown by His explicitly stating after this verse and explaining those corruptions: ﴿Had they gone out with you, they would only have added to you nothing but confusion﴾ [At-Tawba: 47]. The remaining question is: since the more correct and beneficial course was that they should not go out, why did He rebuke the Messenger for granting permission? We say: we have reported from Abu Muslim that he said: there is no indication in His words "Why did you grant them permission?" that the Prophet, peace be upon him, had granted them permission to remain behind. Rather, it is possible to say that they asked him for permission to go out with him, and he granted them permission. On this reading the objection falls away. Abu Muslim said: the evidence for the correctness of what we have said is that this verse indicates that their going out with him would have been a corruption, so that rebuke must be understood as meaning that he, peace be upon him, granted them permission to go out with him. This is confirmed by other verses, among them His words: ﴿If God brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say: "You will never go out with me, ever."﴾ [At-Tawba: 83]. And among them His words: ﴿Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out for the spoils…﴾ [Al-Fath: 15] up to His words: ﴿Say: "You will never follow us."﴾ This is the answer to this objection according to the method of Abu Muslim.

The second answer: we grant that the rebuke in His words ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾ was indeed directed at him, because he, peace be upon him, granted them permission to remain behind. We say: that rebuke was not because remaining behind was a corruption, but because his granting them permission, peace be upon him, to remain behind was a corruption. Its explanation comes in several respects:

The first: he, peace be upon him, granted permission before completing the examination and before fully reflecting and pondering. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Why did you grant them permission until it had become clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾

The second: even if he, peace be upon him, had not granted them permission to remain behind, they would have remained behind on their own initiative, and that staying behind would have become a sign of their hypocrisy. When their hypocrisy became evident, the Muslims would have guarded against them and would not have been deceived by their words. But when the Messenger granted permission to remain behind, their hypocrisy remained hidden, and those benefits were lost.

The third: when they asked permission of the Messenger of God ﷺ, he became angry with them and said, as a rebuke: ﴿Sit with those who sit,﴾ as God related at the end of this verse, namely His words: ﴿And it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ Then they seized upon this expression and said: "He has granted us permission." So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾ meaning: why did you mention to them this expression which enabled them to use it as a means of achieving their aim?

The fourth: those who say that ijtihad (independent juristic reasoning) is not permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them, said: he granted permission only on the basis of ijtihad, and that is not permissible, because when they had access to revelation, acting on ijtihad while having access to revelation is like acting on ijtihad when there is an explicit text. Just as that is impermissible, so is this.

The second issue: the Mu'tazila of Basra (al-Mu'tazila al-Basriyya) said: the verse indicates that He, exalted is He, is described by the attribute of will (muridiyya) and also by the attribute of aversion (karahiyya), as is shown by His words: ﴿But God disliked their setting out.﴾ Our companions said: the meaning of ''God disliked'' is that He willed the absence of that thing. The Basrans said: absence cannot be the object of a relation, because will is an attribute that requires the preponderance of one of the two possibilities over the other, and absence is pure negation. Moreover, a continuous absence cannot be the object of will, because making what already exists come into being again is impossible, and making absence into absence is impossible. Thus it is established that the relation of will to absence is impossible, so it is impermissible to say that what is meant by aversion is the willing of absence.

Our companions replied: we interpret aversion with respect to God as the willing of the opposite of that thing. Thus He, exalted is He, willed that they remain still, and the expression of this will was made by saying that He, exalted is He, disliked their going out with the Messenger.

The third issue: our companions argued on the question of divine decree and predestination (al-qada' wa'l-qadar) from His words: ﴿so He held them back﴾, meaning: He made them sluggish and weakened their desire to set out. The summary of the discussion on this point cannot be complete unless we state the truth clearly: the occurrence of an act depends on the arising of the motive for it. When the motive becomes weak and outweighed, the act cannot proceed from it. Then, whether the motive becomes firm or weak is either from the servant, which would lead to an infinite regress (tasalsul), or from God, in which case the intended conclusion follows, because strengthening the motive comes only from God. When that strengthening occurs, the act must follow, and in that case our statement on the question of divine decree and predestination is valid. Then He, exalted is He, concluded the verse with His words: ﴿And it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ On this there are two issues:

Issue 1: The purpose of this statement is to alert to their blame and to associate them with women, children, and the infirm, whose custom is sitting in their homes. They are the ones who sit back and the ones who remain behind (al-khalifun wa'l-khawalif), as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿They were content to be with those who remain behind﴾ [al-Tawbah: 87].

Issue 2: Scholars differed over who said this statement. It is possible that the speaker was Satan, by way of whispering (waswasah). It is possible that some of them said it to others when they wanted to gather together in staying behind, because whoever undertakes corruption loves to multiply its kinds. It is possible that the speaker was the Messenger (ﷺ) when he gave them permission to stay behind, and so Allah rebuked him. It is possible that the speaker was Allah, glorified is He, because He disliked their going out for corruption, and the meaning was: if you are corrupters, then Allah dislikes your setting out in this manner, so He commanded you to sit back from this particular going out.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 47:

Then He clarified that with His words, exalted is He, after that: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption, and they would have hurried about between you, seeking to cause you fitnah (discord). And among you there are those who listen to them. And Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

Know that in this verse He, exalted is He, clarified the kinds of corruption resulting from their going forth, and they are three. The first is His words: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption (khabal)﴾, and concerning it there are several issues:

The first issue: al-khabal is evil and corruption in everything. From it, madness (al-ata) is called khabal, and the madman is called makhbul. The exegetes have various expressions. Al-Kalbi said: "except evil"; Yaman said: "except deceit"; it was said: "except error (ghayy)"; al-Dahhak said: "except treachery". It was also said: khabal is disturbance in opinion, through making a matter appear attractive to one group and repugnant to another, so that they disagree and their word is divided.

The second issue: Some of the grammarians said: His words ﴿except corruption﴾ are an exceptive of the disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), which is when the excepted item is not of the same genus as the item excepted from. Like your saying: "They increased you in nothing good except corruption." Here the item excepted from is not mentioned, and when it is not mentioned, the exception falls from the more general, and the more general is "thing", so the exception is connected (muttasil), and the sense is: "They increased you in nothing except corruption."

The third issue: The Mu'tazilah said: He, exalted is He, clarified in the first verse that He disliked their being roused, and clarified in this verse that He disliked that rousing only because it includes this corruption, evil and fitnah. That indicates that He, exalted is He, dislikes evil, fitnah and corruption absolutely, and is not pleased except with good, and wills only obedience.

The second kind of corruption arising from their going forth is His words, exalted is He: ﴿and they would have hurried about between you, seeking to cause you fitnah﴾. Concerning "iydā'" (hurrying about) there are two views, transmitted by al-Wahidi:

The first view, which is the view of most lexicographers: iydā' is making a camel run. It is not permissible to say "awda'a al-rajul" if he travels by himself swiftly. One says: "wada'a al-ba'ir" when it runs, and "awda'ahu al-rakib" when the rider makes it run. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say: "wada'at al-naqah" and "awda'a al-rakib", and sometimes they say of the rider: "wada'a".

The second view, which is the view of al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubayd: it is permissible to say "awda'a al-rajul" if he travels by himself swiftly, without meaning that he made his she-camel run. Abu 'Ubayd related that the Prophet (ﷺ) departed from 'Arafah with tranquility upon him, and "awda'a" in the valley of Muhassir. Labid said:

"We are hastening toward a decree of the unseen, and we feed on food and drink."

He meant "hurrying" (musri'in), and it is not permissible that he meant "making camels run", because he did not mean travel on the road. 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah said:

"They were distracted by hostility when they recognized me, and they said: a transgressor who has tired and hurried."

Al-Wahidi said: The verse supports the view of al-Akhfash and Abu 'Ubayd.

Page 66
Know that according to both views, the intended meaning of the verse is running between the Muslims with incitement and tale-bearing. If we adopt the first view, the meaning is: "they would have made their mounts run among you," and the intended sense is hastening with tale-bearing, because the rider is faster than the walker. If we adopt the second view, the intended meaning is that they would hasten in this incitement.

The fourth issue: The author of al-Kashshaf related from Ibn al-Zubayr that he recited "wa-la-awqasu" from "waqasat al-naqah waqsan" when she hastened, and "awqastuha". It was also read "wa-la-arfadu".

If it is asked: How was "wa-la-awda'u" written in the mushaf with the addition of an alif?

The author of al-Kashshaf answered that the fatha was an alif before the Arabic script, and the Arabic script was invented shortly before the revelation of the Qur'an, and a trace of that alif remained in natural habit, so they wrote the form of the hamzah as an alif and its fatha as another alif. Similar to it is: "awla la-adhbahannahu".

The fifth issue: His words ﴿khilalakum﴾ mean "among you (fima baynakum)". From it is His words: ﴿And We caused rivers to gush forth within them (khilalahuma)﴾ [al-Kahf: 33], and His words: ﴿and they went through the houses (khilal al-diyar)﴾ [al-Isra': 5]. Its root is from khalal, which is the gap between two things, and its plural is khilal. From it is His words: ﴿You see the rain come forth from within it (khilalihi)﴾ [al-Nur: 43]. It was read "min khalalihi", and these are the outlets of the falling rain. Al-Asma'i said: "takhallaltu al-qawm" when you enter between their gaps and between them. One says: "We sat among (khilal) the houses of the quarter, and among their dwellings," meaning we sat between the houses and in the midst of the dwellings.

Having known this, we say: His words ﴿they would have hurried about between you (khilalakum)﴾ mean with tale-bearing and corruption. His words ﴿seeking to cause you fitnah﴾ mean they seek on your behalf. Al-Asma'i said: "ibghini kadha" means "seek it for me", and the meaning of "ibghini" and "ibgh li" is the same; and if one says "ibghini", its meaning is "help me with what I seek". The meaning of "fitnah" here is the splitting of the word and the appearance of confusion.

Know that the sum of the statement is that if they went forth among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption, and khabal is the corruption that necessitates difference of opinion, and it is among the greatest matters to be guarded against in wars, because when disagreement in opinion occurs, defeat and breaking arise in the easiest manner. Then He, exalted is He, clarified that they do not restrict themselves to that, but walk among the leaders with tale-bearing, so the corruption becomes greater, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿they would have hurried about between you﴾.

As for His words ﴿and among you there are those who listen to them﴾, there are two views: The first: the intended meaning is: among you there are spies for them who convey to them what they hear from you. This is the view of Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. The second: Qatadah said: among you are those who listen to their speech and accept their word; so when they cast at them kinds of words that necessitate weakness of heart, they accept them, and because of them they slacken from standing by the command of jihad as it should be.

If it is asked: How is that permissible for believers given the strength of their religion and their intention in jihad?

We say: It is not impossible that the word of the hypocrites affects those whose faith is recent. It is not impossible that some people are naturally disposed to cowardice, weakness and faintness of heart, so their words affect them. It is not impossible that some Muslims are relatives of the leaders of the hypocrites, so they look at them with eyes of reverence and honor, and for this reason the words of these great hypocrites affect them. It is also not impossible to say: the hypocrites are of two kinds: some are limited to hypocrisy and do not strive in the land with corruption; then the second group of hypocrites urge them to strive in corruption by casting doubts and rumors upon them.

Page 67
Then He, exalted is He, concluded the verse with His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, who wronged themselves through their disbelief and hypocrisy, and wronged others by striving to cast others into the forms of calamities and violations. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verses 48–50:

The verse of God Most High: ﴿Indeed they had sought discord before, and had upset affairs for you until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me." Surely they have fallen into temptation already, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers.﴾

Know that what is mentioned in this verse is another kind of the scheming of the hypocrites and the corruption of their inner selves. He says: ﴿They had sought discord before﴾, meaning: before the event of Tabuk. Ibn Jurayj said: this refers to twelve men from among the hypocrites who stood at the Thaniyyat al-Wada' on the night of al-Aqabah in order to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said that what is meant is what Abdullah ibn Ubayy did on the Day of Uhud, when he turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ) with his companions. It was also said: they sought to turn your companions away from the religion, to return them to disbelief, and to dissuade people from you. The meaning of fitnah (discord, a trial that sows division; a gloss: the strife that causes separation after unity) is the disagreement that causes division after harmony, and this is what the hypocrites sought for the Muslims, but God protected them from it. His saying ﴿and had upset affairs for you﴾: taqlib al-amr (the turning over of a matter) is turning it about and reconsidering it for the sake of reflection and deliberation. The meaning is: they strove in devising schemes against you and plotting against you. It is said of a man who manages the aspects of stratagems: "So-and-so is a ḥawwal qallab," meaning he turns himself about in the aspects of stratagems.

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse﴾. The meaning is: these hypocrites were persistent in the way of plotting, deceit, stirring up strife, and turning people away from accepting the religion, until the truth came, which had been in the position of doctrines (al-madhahib), and what is meant by it is the Qur'an and the call of Muhammad. ﴿And the command of God prevailed﴾, which had been as if hidden. What is meant by the command of God is the causes that God Most High manifested and made influential in strengthening the law of Muhammad, upon him be peace. ﴿While they were averse﴾: that is, they were averse to the coming of this truth and the prevailing of the command of God. In this there is an admonition that their plotting, their scheming, and their exertion in stirring up evil have no effect, for they have been seeking this deceit and scheming from the beginning, while God has turned it back upon their own necks, reversed their intention, and brought the opposite of their aim. Since the matter was so in the past, it will be so in the future.

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾. He means: "Grant me leave to remain behind, and do not tempt me by means of the command to go out." They mentioned several interpretations of this:

The first: "do not tempt me," meaning: do not cause me to fall into fitnah, which is sin, by not granting me leave. For if you forbid me from staying behind and I stay without your permission, I will fall into sin. According to this interpretation, it is possible that they said this in mockery, and it is also possible that they said it in earnest. And if that man was a hypocrite, his assumption would prevail that Muhammad, peace be upon him, was truthful, though he was not certain of that.

The second: "do not tempt me," meaning: do not cast me into destruction, for the time is one of intense heat and I have no strength for it.

The third: "do not tempt me, for if I go out with you my wealth and my family will perish."

The fourth: Jadd ibn Qays said: "The Ansar know that I am greatly attached to women; so do not tempt me with the daughters of al-Asfar" (meaning the women of the Byzantines), "but I will help you with wealth, so leave me." It was also read: ﴿ولا تُفْتِنِّي﴾ (wa-la tuftinni), from aftanahu.

﴿Surely they have fallen into temptation already﴾: the meaning is that they guard against falling into fitnah, yet in fact they have already fallen into nothing but fitnah, for the greatest kind of fitnah is disbelief in God and His Messenger, and rebellion against accepting the obligations. Moreover, they remain apart from the Muslims, fearing that God will expose them and send down verses explaining their hypocrisy. In the mushaf of Ubayy (Ubayy ibn Ka'b) the reading is "saqata" (singular), because the word man (whoever), though singular in form, is plural in meaning. The people of the ma'ani (the scholars of rhetorical meaning) said: In this there is an admonition that whoever disobeys God for some purpose, God will nullify that purpose for him. Do you not see that these people chose to stay behind only so as not to fall into fitnah, yet God made clear that they are actually falling into the very fitnah and are among the fallen?

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾. It was said: it will encompass them on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the causes of that encompassing are already present in the present, so it is as though they are in its midst. The Islamic philosophers (al-hukama' al-islamiyyah, a gloss: the Muslim philosophers) said: they were deprived of the light of the knowledge of God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. They did not believe that they had any perfection or happiness apart from this world and what is in it of wealth and status. Moreover, they became known among people for hypocrisy, for disparaging the religion, and for intending every evil against the Messenger. They saw that the dominion of Islam was forever rising, ascending, and increasing, while they were in the greatest fear for themselves, their children, and their wealth. The sum is that they were deprived of all spiritual felicities, so they were in the most intense fear because of immediate circumstances, and intense fear combined with intense ignorance is the greatest kind of spiritual punishment. So God Most High expressed those states by His saying: ﴿And indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verses 48–50:

The verse of God Most High: ﴿Indeed they had sought discord before, and had upset affairs for you until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me." Surely they have fallen into temptation already, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers.﴾

Know that what is mentioned in this verse is another kind of the scheming of the hypocrites and the corruption of their inner selves. He says: ﴿They had sought discord before﴾, meaning: before the event of Tabuk. Ibn Jurayj said: this refers to twelve men from among the hypocrites who stood at the Thaniyyat al-Wada' on the night of al-Aqabah in order to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said that what is meant is what Abdullah ibn Ubayy did on the Day of Uhud, when he turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ) with his companions. It was also said: they sought to turn your companions away from the religion, to return them to disbelief, and to dissuade people from you. The meaning of fitnah (discord, a trial that sows division; a gloss: the strife that causes separation after unity) is the disagreement that causes division after harmony, and this is what the hypocrites sought for the Muslims, but God protected them from it. His saying ﴿and had upset affairs for you﴾: taqlib al-amr (the turning over of a matter) is turning it about and reconsidering it for the sake of reflection and deliberation. The meaning is: they strove in devising schemes against you and plotting against you. It is said of a man who manages the aspects of stratagems: "So-and-so is a ḥawwal qallab," meaning he turns himself about in the aspects of stratagems.

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse﴾. The meaning is: these hypocrites were persistent in the way of plotting, deceit, stirring up strife, and turning people away from accepting the religion, until the truth came, which had been in the position of doctrines (al-madhahib), and what is meant by it is the Qur'an and the call of Muhammad. ﴿And the command of God prevailed﴾, which had been as if hidden. What is meant by the command of God is the causes that God Most High manifested and made influential in strengthening the law of Muhammad, upon him be peace. ﴿While they were averse﴾: that is, they were averse to the coming of this truth and the prevailing of the command of God. In this there is an admonition that their plotting, their scheming, and their exertion in stirring up evil have no effect, for they have been seeking this deceit and scheming from the beginning, while God has turned it back upon their own necks, reversed their intention, and brought the opposite of their aim. Since the matter was so in the past, it will be so in the future.

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾. He means: "Grant me leave to remain behind, and do not tempt me by means of the command to go out." They mentioned several interpretations of this:

The first: "do not tempt me," meaning: do not cause me to fall into fitnah, which is sin, by not granting me leave. For if you forbid me from staying behind and I stay without your permission, I will fall into sin. According to this interpretation, it is possible that they said this in mockery, and it is also possible that they said it in earnest. And if that man was a hypocrite, his assumption would prevail that Muhammad, peace be upon him, was truthful, though he was not certain of that.

The second: "do not tempt me," meaning: do not cast me into destruction, for the time is one of intense heat and I have no strength for it.

The third: "do not tempt me, for if I go out with you my wealth and my family will perish."

The fourth: Jadd ibn Qays said: "The Ansar know that I am greatly attached to women; so do not tempt me with the daughters of al-Asfar" (meaning the women of the Byzantines), "but I will help you with wealth, so leave me." It was also read: ﴿ولا تُفْتِنِّي﴾ (wa-la tuftinni), from aftanahu.

﴿Surely they have fallen into temptation already﴾: the meaning is that they guard against falling into fitnah, yet in fact they have already fallen into nothing but fitnah, for the greatest kind of fitnah is disbelief in God and His Messenger, and rebellion against accepting the obligations. Moreover, they remain apart from the Muslims, fearing that God will expose them and send down verses explaining their hypocrisy. In the mushaf of Ubayy (Ubayy ibn Ka'b) the reading is "saqata" (singular), because the word man (whoever), though singular in form, is plural in meaning. The people of the ma'ani (the scholars of rhetorical meaning) said: In this there is an admonition that whoever disobeys God for some purpose, God will nullify that purpose for him. Do you not see that these people chose to stay behind only so as not to fall into fitnah, yet God made clear that they are actually falling into the very fitnah and are among the fallen?

Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾. It was said: it will encompass them on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the causes of that encompassing are already present in the present, so it is as though they are in its midst. The Islamic philosophers (al-hukama' al-islamiyyah, a gloss: the Muslim philosophers) said: they were deprived of the light of the knowledge of God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. They did not believe that they had any perfection or happiness apart from this world and what is in it of wealth and status. Moreover, they became known among people for hypocrisy, for disparaging the religion, and for intending every evil against the Messenger. They saw that the dominion of Islam was forever rising, ascending, and increasing, while they were in the greatest fear for themselves, their children, and their wealth. The sum is that they were deprived of all spiritual felicities, so they were in the most intense fear because of immediate circumstances, and intense fear combined with intense ignorance is the greatest kind of spiritual punishment. So God Most High expressed those states by His saying: ﴿And indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾.

The verse of God Most High: ﴿Indeed they had sought discord before, and had upset affairs for you until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me." Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; and if a calamity strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution beforehand," and they turn away while they rejoice.﴾ ﴿Say: "Nothing will ever strike us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector (mawla), and upon Allah let the believers rely."﴾

Know that this is another kind of the scheming of the hypocrites (munafiqin) and of the corruption of their inner selves. The meaning is: if good befalls you in some of the military campaigns, whether it is victory, or booty, or the submission of some of the kings of the borderlands, it distresses them. And if a calamity strikes you, such as a disaster, hardship, misfortune, or something hateful, they rejoice at it and say, "We had already taken our affair, which we are known for, namely caution, vigilance and acting with resolve, ﴿beforehand﴾." That is, before what has happened occurred. And they turn away from the place of discussing this and gathering for it, to their families, while they are rejoicing and delighted.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that the good was on the day of Badr and the calamity on the day of Uhud. If it is established by a report that this is what is meant, then it is obligatory to adopt it; otherwise, it is necessary to apply it to every good and every calamity, since it is known from the condition of the hypocrites that in every good and at every calamity they are described by the attribute that God mentions here.

Then Exalted is He said: ﴿Say: "Nothing will ever strike us except what Allah has decreed for us."﴾ There are several opinions concerning this:

The first opinion: the meaning is that nothing good or bad, nor fear or hope, nor hardship or ease, will befall us except that it is predetermined for us and written with Allah. That it is written with Allah indicates that it is known to Allah and decreed by Him, for everything else is possible (mumkin), and the possible is not preponderated except by the preponderation of the Necessary (wajib), and all possible things ultimately terminate in His decree and His measure.

Know that our companions (the Ash'aris) cling to this verse in holding that the decree of Allah encompasses all created things, and that a change of a thing from what Allah has decreed is impossible. The explanation of this statement is in several aspects:

The first: the existent is either necessary or possible, and the possible is impossible for one of its two sides to be preponderated over the other by itself; therefore it must terminate in the preponderation of the Necessary by its essence, and everything else is necessary through His bringing it into being, His influence and His creating it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The pen has dried with what will be until the Day of Resurrection."

The second: since Allah, exalted is He, wrote all the states in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), He has known them and judged them. So if the matter were to occur contrary to them, it would necessarily follow that knowledge would turn into ignorance and true judgment into falsehood, and all of that is impossible. We have elaborated on the explanation of this argument in the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6].

If it is said: He, exalted is He, only mentioned this statement to console the Messenger for their rejoicing at his grief and his hardships, so what connection does this doctrine have with that?

We say: The reason for it is his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever knows the secret of Allah in the decree, calamities become easy for him." For when a person knows that what has occurred could not have failed to occur, the struggle leaves the soul and contentment with it is attained.

The second opinion regarding the interpretation of this verse is that the meaning of: ﴿Nothing will ever strike us except what Allah has decreed for us﴾ is: in the outcome of our affair, of victory over the enemy and gaining dominion over them. The aim is that it becomes apparent to the hypocrites that although the states of the Messenger and the Muslims differ in happiness and sorrow, yet in the end the dominion, the conquest and the victory are on their side; this will be a vexation to the hypocrites and a refutation of them in that rejoicing.

The third opinion: al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that when we are overcome, we become deserving of a great reward and abundant recompense, and if we are victorious, we become deserving of recompense in the Hereafter, and we succeed with abundant wealth and beautiful praise in this world. And since this is the case, those calamities and griefs become bearable in comparison with attaining these lofty ranks. Although these opinions are good, the sound and correct truth is the first.

Then Exalted is He said: ﴿He is our Protector (mawla)﴾, and what is intended by it is what our companions say: that it is good for Him, exalted is He, to dispose of the world as He wills, and to will for the sake of the fact that He is their Owner and their Creator, and because there is no objection to Him in any of His acts. This statement thus applies to what preceded; and for this reason we say: even if He, exalted is He, brings upon some of His servants various kinds of calamities, it is obligatory to be content with them, because He, exalted is He, is their Mawla and they are His servants; so those dispositions are good from Him merely by virtue of His being their Mawla, and no one has any objection to Him in any of His acts.

Then Exalted is He said: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ Its meaning: even though nothing is obligatory upon Him toward any of His servants, nor any matter among matters, yet despite this He is of great mercy, abundant grace and benevolence; therefore the believer must in principle rely upon none but Him, and cut off his hope except from His grace and mercy. For His saying: ﴿upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ conveys restriction (hasr), and this is like an alert that the condition of the hypocrites is the opposite of this, and that they rely only upon worldly means and fleeting, transient pleasures.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 52:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things (al-husnayayn), while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you."﴾

Know that this is the second answer concerning the joy of the hypocrites at the misfortunes of the believers. That is because when a Muslim goes out to fight, if he becomes defeated and killed, he gains a good name in this world and the great reward which Allah has prepared for the martyrs in the Hereafter. And if he becomes victorious, he gains in this world lawful wealth and a beautiful name, which is manliness, strength and power, and in the Hereafter the great reward. As for the hypocrite, if he sits in his house, then in the present he sits in his house blameworthy, ascribed to cowardice, feebleness, weakness of heart, and contentment with base worldly matters, in a manner in which women, children and those incapable among women share with him. Then they will always be fearful for their own selves, their children and their wealth. And in the Hereafter, if they die, they have passed to the everlasting punishment on the Day of Resurrection; and if Allah permits their killing, they fall into killing, captivity and plunder, and they pass from this world to the punishment of the Fire. So the hypocrite does not await for the believer anything but one of the two mentioned states, and each one of them is in the utmost of majesty, elevation and honour. And the Muslim awaits for the hypocrite one of the two mentioned states, namely remaining in this world along with disgrace, humiliation and abasement, then passing to the punishment of the Resurrection, or falling into killing and plunder along with disgrace and humiliation. And each of these two states is in the utmost of baseness and vileness. Then Allah, exalted is He, said to the hypocrites: ﴿So wait﴾ for us one of the two noble states, ﴿indeed, we are waiting with you﴾ for your falling into one of the two base and descending states.

Al-Wahidi said: It is said: "So-and-so awaits misfortunes for so-and-so" when he is waiting for an adversity to befall him, and this has already been discussed. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: al-tarabbus is holding fast to something for which one waits until its time comes; therefore it is said: "So-and-so hoards (yatarabbas) food" when he holds on to it until its price rises. Al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan (the best). They differed in the interpretation of His saying: ﴿with a punishment from Him or at our hands﴾. It was said: from Allah, that is, a punishment which Allah sends down upon them in this world, or at our hands, by Him permitting us to kill you. And it was said: a punishment from Allah which encompasses the punishment of this world and the Hereafter, or at our hands, the killing.

If it is said: if they are hypocrites, it is not permitted to kill them while they display faith, so how does He, exalted is He, say that?

We say: al-Hasan said: the meaning of "at our hands" is if your hypocrisy becomes manifest, for when their hypocrisy becomes manifest they are like the other polytheists in being at war with the believers. And His saying ﴿So wait﴾, although it is in the form of a command, its meaning is threat, as in His saying: ﴿Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49]. And Allah knows best.

[Page 71]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."﴾

Know that when the Exalted explained in the first verse that the end of these hypocrites is punishment in this world and in the Hereafter, He explained that even if they perform some of the deeds of righteousness, they will not benefit from them in the Hereafter. The purpose is to make clear that the causes of punishment in this world and the Hereafter are combined against them, and that the causes of comfort and good are removed from them in this world and in the Hereafter. There are several issues in this verse.

Issue One: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read كُرْهًا (kurhan) here, and in Surah al-Nisa' and al-Ahqaf, with a damma on the kaf. ʿAsim and Ibn ʿAmir read it with a damma in al-Ahqaf, meaning "hardship" (al-mashaqqa), and with a fatha in al-Nisa' and al-Tawbah, meaning "compulsion" (al-ikrah). The rest read it with a fatha on the kaf in all of these places. It is said that both are dialectal variants. It is also said that the damma indicates hardship, and the fatha indicates what one is compelled to do.

Issue Two: Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was revealed concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays, when he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Permit me to remain behind, and this is my wealth; I will help you with it."

Know that although the occasion of revelation is specific, the ruling is general. His words ﴿Spend willingly or unwillingly﴾, although their wording is that of a command, their meaning is that of a conditional and its consequence. The meaning is: whether you spend willingly or under compulsion, that will never be accepted from you.

Know that a statement (khabar) and a command (amr) are close in meaning, so it is fitting for each of them to take the place of the other. As for placing a command in the position of a statement, it is as here, and as in His words: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80], and His words: ﴿Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension﴾ [Maryam: 75]. As for placing a statement in the position of a command, it is like His words: ﴿And mothers breastfeed their children﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], and ﴿And divorced women await by themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. Kuthayyir said:

"Be harsh with us or be kind; there is no reproach from us for her, and she is not shunned if she turns away."

His words ﴿Spend willingly or unwillingly﴾ mean: "willing" (ṭāʾiʿīn) or "unwilling" (kārihīn). In this there are two interpretations.

The first: willing, without obligation from Allah and His Messenger, or unwilling, under compulsion from Allah and His Messenger. He called the obligation "compulsion" because they were hypocrites, so Allah's obligating them to spend was burdensome to them, like compulsion.

The second: the meaning is "willing, without compulsion from your leaders," because the leaders of the hypocrites used to drive their followers to spend for what they saw as a benefit in it, or "unwilling, under compulsion from their side."

Then the Exalted said: ﴿It will never be accepted from you﴾. This may mean that the Messenger (ﷺ) will not accept those wealths from them, and it may mean that they will not become accepted in the sight of Allah.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people﴾. This indicates that the non-acceptance is caused by their being in a state of fisq (grave disobedience, moral corruption).

Al-Jubba'i said: the verse shows that fisq nullifies acts of obedience, because the Exalted explained that their expenditure is absolutely not accepted, and He attributed that to their being fasiqun. The meaning of acceptance (taqabbul) is reward and praise. When that is not accepted, its meaning is that there is no reward and no praise. Since He attributed this to fisq, it indicates that fisq affects the removal of this meaning. Then al-Jubba'i reinforced this with their well-known proof on this question: that fisq necessitates everlasting blame and punishment, while obedience necessitates everlasting praise and reward, and combining the two is impossible. Therefore combining the two entitlements is impossible.

Know that he should not have mentioned this argument after Allah had removed this doubt in the most eloquent way, namely His words: ﴿Nothing prevented them from having their expenditures accepted except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 54]. Here the Exalted made clear, by this explicit wording, that nothing prevents the acceptance of these deeds except disbelief. At this point, this statement becomes one of the clearest proofs that fisq does not nullify acts of obedience. When He said: ﴿Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people﴾, it was as if a questioner asked: "Is this ruling caused by the general fact that those deeds are fisq, or by the specific fact that those deeds are described by that fisq?" The Exalted then made clear what removes this doubt: non-acceptance is not caused by the general fact that it is fisq, but by its specific attribute, which is that this fisq is disbelief (kufr). Thus it is established that this argument is invalid.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verse 54:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling.﴾

And in this there are issues:

The first issue: The explicit meaning of this verse indicates that wickedness (fisq) has no effect insofar as it is wickedness in this prevention, and this is explicit in refuting the view of the Mu'tazilah, as we have summarized and explained it.

The second issue: The apparent wording indicates that the prevention of acceptance is due to the combination of the three matters: disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, not coming to the prayer except in a state of laziness, and spending in a manner of aversion.

One might say: Disbelief in Allah is an independent cause for the prevention of acceptance, and when an independent cause is present, nothing else retains any effect. So how is it possible to attribute this ruling to the remaining two causes?

The answer: This objection applies only to the view of the Mu'tazilah, who said that disbelief, by virtue of being disbelief, has an effect on this ruling. As for us, none of the acts necessarily entails reward or punishment at all; rather, they are only indicators (mu'arrifat), and the gathering of many indicators upon one thing is impossible. Rather, we say: this is among the strongest certain proofs that these acts do not have an effect on these rulings, for reasons pertaining to them. The proof for this is that He, exalted is He, stated that these three matters occurred in their case. If each one of them were a complete cause of this ruling, it would follow that independent causes would converge upon one single effect, and that is impossible, because the effect would be independent of each one of them, so its need for them all together would follow at the very time of its independence from them all together, and that is impossible. Thus it is established that the claim that these acts have an effect on these rulings leads to this impossibility, so that claim is invalid.

The third issue: This verse indicates that none of the acts of righteousness is accepted by Allah together with disbelief in Allah.

If it is said: How then is this to be reconciled with His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7]?

We say: That must be interpreted as referring to its effect in lightening the punishment. The verse also indicates that the prayer is obligatory upon the disbeliever, for otherwise Allah would not have blamed them for performing it in a state of laziness.

Page 73
If they say: Why can it not be said that what necessitates blame is not abandoning the prayer? Rather, what necessitates blame is performing it in a state of laziness, treating it like the rest of their conduct such as standing and sitting. And just as their sitting in a state of laziness does not prevent the acceptance of their obedience, likewise their prayer would have been required of them had it not been obligatory upon them.

The fourth issue: The explanation of "kusala" (lazy) has passed in Surat al-Nisa'. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "kusala", with a damma and with a fatha, is the plural of kaslan, like sukara and hayara are plurals of sakran and hayran. The exegetes said: This laziness means that if he is in a congregation, he prays, and if he is alone, he does not pray. The author (al-Razi) said: This meaning only affects the prevention of the acceptance of acts of obedience because this meaning indicates that he does not pray in obedience to the command of Allah, but prays only out of fear of people's blame, and this degree alone does not indicate disbelief. But when Allah mentioned it after describing them with disbelief, it indicates that the laziness was only because they believed that it was not obligatory, and this necessitates disbelief.

As for His saying: ﴿and they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾, the meaning is: they do not spend for the purpose of obedience, but only for the sake of an apparent benefit. That is because they used to regard spending as a loss and a waste among themselves. This requires that the soul be content when paying zakat and spending in the way of Allah, because Allah, exalted is He, blamed the hypocrites for their aversion to spending. This is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: "Pay the zakat of your wealth with your souls content therewith." If one pays it while being averse to it, that is among the signs of disbelief and hypocrisy. The author, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The essence of these discussions indicates that the spirit of acts of obedience is performing them for the purpose of servitude and submission in obedience. If they are not performed for this purpose, there is no benefit in them, and indeed they may become a burden upon their doer.

The fifth issue: ﴿Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "an yuqbala" with the ya', and the rest read it with the ta' on account of the feminine. The reasoning of the first two: the nafaqat (contributions) carry the meaning of infaq (spending), as in His saying: ﴿So whoever receives an admonition﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]. The reasoning of the one who reads with the ta' is that the verb is attributed to a feminine noun. The author of al-Kashshaf said: It has been read "nafaqatuhum" and "nafaqatuhum", in the plural and the singular. And al-Sulami read "an yaqbala minhum nafaqatihim", with the verb attributed to Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

[p. 74] Consider that when God, in the previous verse, cut off the hope of the hypocrites from all the benefits of the Hereafter, He then explained that the things they regard as benefits in this world are in fact causes of their punishment. He made them the means by which they are held in esteem in this world, and also the means by which trials and calamities gather around them. Whoever reflects on these verses will see that they are arranged in the best possible order. God first described their vile deeds and disgraceful actions, then described the severe punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter and the forms of affliction and tribulation they face in this world. He then explained that the acts of righteousness they perform will benefit them nothing on the Day of Resurrection. In this verse, He explained that what they think is a benefit of this world is in reality a cause of their torment, their suffering, and the intensification of their trial. At this point it becomes clear

[p. 74] that hypocrisy brings about every calamity in religion and in this world, and nullifies every good in religion and in this world. When a person understands this order, he knows that the speech could not be arranged in a better way than this. Success is from God. The following are some issues concerning this verse:

The first issue: Although this address is apparently directed specifically to the Messenger (peace be upon him), what is meant by it is all the believers. That is, one should not be impressed by the wealth of these hypocrites and disbelievers, nor by their children, nor by any other of God's blessings upon them. A parallel to this is God's words: ﴿And do not extend your eyes…﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:131].

The second issue: Al-i'jab (admiration, being impressed) is joy in a thing combined with a kind of pride in it, and with the belief that no one else possesses anything equal to it. This state indicates that the soul is absorbed in that thing and cut off from God. It is not far, in God's judgment, that He should remove that thing from that person and give it to someone else. Whenever a person remembers this meaning, his admiration for the thing disappears. For this reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Three things are destructive: stinginess that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and a man's admiration of himself." The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say: "Those who accumulate wealth are ruined." He (peace be upon him) also said: "What is yours of your wealth is only what you ate and consumed, or what you wore and wore out, or what you gave in charity and sent ahead." Ubayd ibn Umayr mentioned, and traced it back to the Messenger (peace be upon him): "Whoever's wealth increases, his reckoning becomes more severe; whoever's trade increases, his devils multiply; and whoever draws closer to the ruler, moves further from God." Relevant reports on this theme are numerous, and their purpose is to restrain one from relying on this world, and to prevent excessive attachment to its love and pride in it.

Some of the scholars said: Existing things, by rational division, fall into four categories. The first is that which is eternal and everlasting, and that is God, exalted is His majesty. The second is that which is neither eternal nor everlasting, and that is this world. The third is that which is eternal but not everlasting, and this is impossible to exist, because it has been established by proof that whatever is proven to have no beginning is impossible to cease. The fourth is that which is everlasting but not eternal, and that is the Hereafter and all accountable beings. For the Hereafter has a beginning but no end, and likewise the accountable person, whether obedient or disobedient, has a beginning to his life but no end to it.

When this is established, it follows that the relationship between the accountable human being and the Hereafter is stronger than his relationship with this world. From this it is apparent that he was created for the Hereafter and not for this world. Therefore he should not be excessively impressed with this world, nor should his heart incline toward it, for his original dwelling is the Hereafter, not this world.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends…﴾, there are the following issues:

The first issue: The grammarians said: There is an ellipsis in the verse, as if it were said: "Allah only intends to give them respite through them, so that He may punish them." It is also permissible that this lam (the particle "li-") has the meaning of "an" (that), like His words: ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you…﴾ [al-Nisa 4:26], that is: "that He may make clear to you."

The second issue: Mujahid, al-Suddi and Qatadah said: There is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, rearrangement of word order) in the verse. The intended meaning is: "So let not their wealth or their children impress you in the life of this world. Allah only intends to punish them through them in the Hereafter." The Qadi said: Here there are two questions. The first is: wealth and children are not a punishment; rather, they are among the blessings with which God has favored His servants. Therefore these scholars resorted to the inversion. However, this resort does not answer the question, because it would still be asked after this inversion: how can wealth and children be a punishment?

[p. 75] So they must posit an omission in the speech, by saying: "He intends to punish them through them insofar as they were a cause of punishment." Once they say this, they no longer need the inversion, because it would be correct to say: "Allah intends to punish them through them in this world, insofar as they were a cause of punishment." Also, if He had said: "So let not their wealth or their children impress you in the life of this world," this addition would have little benefit, because it is well known that admiration for wealth and children exists only in this world, whereas the situation of punishment is not so restricted, for it may exist in this world just as it does in the Hereafter. Thus it is established that this claim of inversion is worthless.

The third issue: Wealth and children may be a cause of punishment in this world, and they may be a cause of punishment in the Hereafter. As for their being a cause of punishment in this world, this is for several reasons:

The first: Whoever's love for a thing is stronger and more intense, his grief and the pain of his heart over its loss are greater and more difficult, and his fear of its loss is more severe and more painful. Those who have acquired abundant wealth and children, if those things remain with them, are in the pain of intense fear of losing them; and if they are lost and perish, they are in the pain of intense grief because of their loss. Thus it is established that the acquisition of the causes of bodily happiness cannot be separated from this heart: either because of fear of their loss, or because of grief at their loss.

The second: Acquiring and obtaining these things requires great exertion and immense hardship, and then, once they are obtained, they require far greater, harder, more difficult, and more burdensome efforts to preserve them. So preserving wealth after obtaining it is more difficult than acquiring it. Therefore the one who is infatuated with wealth and children is always in the toil of guarding and protecting them from ruin. Moreover, he benefits only from a small part of that wealth. So the toil is great and the benefit is small.

The third: When a person's love for these wealth and children is great, either these wealth and children will remain with him until the end of his life, or they will not remain and will instead perish and be lost. If the first, then at death his grief will be great and his regret intense, because parting from what is beloved is severe, and leaving what is beloved is harder and more difficult. If the second, namely that these things perish and are lost during his lifetime, his sorrow over them grows greater and the pain of his heart becomes more intense because of them. Thus it is established that the possession of wealth and children is a cause of punishment in this world.

The fourth: This world is sweet and green, and the senses incline toward it. When it becomes abundant and continuous, a person becomes absorbed in it, and his soul turns entirely toward it. This becomes a cause of his being deprived of the remembrance of God. Then a kind of hardness, strength and domination arises in his heart, and the more wealth and status he has, the stronger that hardness becomes. To this refers God's words: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq 96:6]. It is thus clear that the abundance of wealth and children is a powerful cause of the disappearance of the love of God and the love of the Hereafter from the heart, and of the arising of love for this world and its desires in the heart. Therefore at death it is as if the person moves from a garden to a prison, from the company of relatives and loved ones to a place of distress and estrangement, so his pain grows and his regret intensifies. Then at the Gathering, what was lawful of it becomes a reckoning, and what was unlawful of it becomes a punishment. Thus it is established that the abundance of wealth and children is a cause of punishment in this world and in the Hereafter.

If it is said: This meaning applies to everyone, so what is the benefit of singling out these hypocrites for this punishment?

We say: The hypocrites are specially characterized by additional factors in this regard:

The first: When a man believes in God and the Last Day, he knows that he was created for the Hereafter and not for this world, and through this knowledge his love for this world weakens. But the hypocrite, since he believes that there is no happiness except in these immediate goods, has a greater desire for them and a stronger love for them, and the pains caused by their loss are greater in his case, and they intensify at the approach of death and the appearance of its signs. This kind of punishment is therefore experienced by them in this world because of their love for wealth and children.

[p. 76] The second: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to require them to spend that wealth in good causes, and to require them to send their wealth and children to jihad and raids. This would necessitate exposing their children to being killed. The people believed that Muhammad was not truthful in being a messenger from God, and they believed that spending that wealth was a waste of it without benefit, and that exposing their children to being killed was taking on this severe hardship without benefit. There is no doubt that this is extremely painful to the heart. So this additional kind of torment was experienced by the hypocrites.

The third: They hated Muhammad (peace be upon him) in their hearts, yet they needed to spend their wealth, their children and their own selves in his service. There is no doubt that this state is extremely burdensome and severe.

The fourth: They were afraid that they would be exposed and that their hypocrisy and disbelief would become completely manifest, so that they would become like the rest of the people of war among the disbelievers, and then the Messenger would target them for killing, the taking of their children captive, and the plundering of their wealth. Whenever a verse was revealed, they feared the manifestation of their disgrace; and whenever the Messenger called them, they feared that he might have discovered some aspect of their deceit and wickedness. All of this necessarily causes the heart to suffer and increases the punishment.

The fifth: Many of the hypocrites had pious children, such as Hanzalah ibn Abi Amir, whom the angels washed, and Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who fought at Badr and was held in high regard by God. These were a great multitude who were free of hypocrisy. They did not approve of their fathers' way of hypocrisy, and they criticised them and opposed them. When a son becomes like this, the father's distress and sense of estrangement from him grow greater. Thus the existence of those children became a cause of their torment.

The sixth: The poor and weak among the Companions went out in the service of the Messenger (peace be upon him) to the raids, then returned with the noble title, great praise and success in gaining booty. Meanwhile these hypocrites, despite their abundant wealth and strong children, remained in the corners of their houses like the disabled and the weak among people. Then people looked at them with eyes of hatred, contempt and branding with hypocrisy. It is as if the abundance of wealth and children became the cause of these conditions. Thus it is established through these aspects that the abundance of their wealth and children became a cause of increased punishment in this world for them.

* * *

The fourth issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued, to establish that everything that comes into existence is willed by God, exalted is He, based on His words: ﴿and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾. They said: The meaning of the verse is that God, exalted is He, willed the departure of their souls while they are in disbelief, and whoever wills that has willed disbelief.

Al-Jubba'i answered and said: The meaning of the verse is that He, exalted is He, willed the taking of their souls while they were disbelievers, and this does not necessitate that He, exalted is He, wills disbelief. Do you not see that a sick person may say to the physician: "I want you to come to me during the time of my illness"? This wanting does not make him one who wills his own illness. And he may say to the physician: "I want you to heal my wound," and this does not necessitate that he wills the occurrence of that wound. And a sultan may say to his army: "Kill the rebels while they are advancing to war," and this does not indicate that he wills that war. So it is likewise here.

The answer: What he said is a remarkable deception. This is because all the examples he cited ultimately reduce to one point, namely that the one who wills wants the removal of that thing. When the sick person says to the physician, "I want you to come to me during the time of my illness," its meaning is: "I want you to strive to remove my illness." When he says to him, "I want you to heal my wound," its meaning is: "I want you to remove this wound from me." When the sultan says, "Kill the rebels while they are advancing to war," its meaning is a request for the removal, nullification, and eradication of that
page 77
warfare. Thus it is established that what is willed and what is requested in all these examples is the annihilation and removal of that thing, so it is impossible that its existence be willed. This is unlike this verse, because the taking of the soul of the disbeliever is not an expression of the removal of his disbelief, nor does it necessitate that removal; rather, they are two matters that are mutually compatible, and there is absolutely no contradiction between them. So when God mentioned in this verse that He willed the taking of their souls while they were disbelievers, it became necessary that He wills their being disbelievers at the time that taking occurs, just as if he said: "I want to meet so-and-so while he is in the house," which necessitates that he wanted him to be in the house. The complete verification in this matter is: the taking of the soul in a state of disbelief cannot occur except at the time disbelief occurs, and whoever wills a thing wills what is necessary to it. So when God willed the taking of the soul during disbelief, and it is established that whoever wills a thing wills all that is necessary to it, it follows that He, exalted is He, wills that disbelief. Thus it is established that the examples cited by al-Jubba'i are pure deception.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 9, verses 56–58:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are fearful.﴾ ﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it while they rush headlong.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that they had gathered every harm of the Hereafter and this world, and were deprived of all the benefits of the Hereafter and this world, He returned to mentioning their ugly deeds and disgraceful acts, and explained their boldness in making false oaths. So He said: ﴿And they swear by Allah﴾, that is, the hypocrites to the believers when they sit with them, ﴿that they are surely of you﴾, that is, upon your religion.

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿But they are not of you﴾, that is, they are not upon your religion, ﴿rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾ of being killed. So they displayed faith and concealed hypocrisy. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14]. The fazaq (fear) is dread, and from it one says: a man who is fearful (faruq), meaning one who is intensely afraid. And among its meanings: if they found a place of escape in which they could take shelter, secure for themselves from you, they would flee to it and separate from you. So do not think that their agreement with you in the abode and dwelling is from the heart. As for His saying: ﴿If they could find a refuge﴾. The malja' (refuge) is the place in which one takes shelter. Similar to it is al-lja' (with a short vowel and hamza), and its root is from laja'a ila kadha yalja'u, laj'an, with fatha on the lam and sukun on the jim. Similarly, iltaja' and alja'tuhu ila kadha, meaning: I made him compelled towards it.

His saying: ﴿or caves﴾. It is the plural of maghara, which is the place into which a person disappears, i.e., conceals himself. Abu 'Ubayd said: every thing into which you pass and vanish is a maghara for you, and from it comes: the water sank into the earth (ghara al-ma'u fi al-ardi) and the spring sank (ghararat al-'ayn).

His saying: ﴿a place to enter﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: its origin is mudtakhal, and the ta' after the dal is changed into dal, because the ta' is voiceless (mahmusah) and the dal is voiced (majhurah), and both come from the same articulation point; it is a mufta'al form from al-dukhul (entering), like al-mutallaj from al-wulij. Its meaning: the path that is hidden by entering into it. Al-Kalbi and Ibn Zayd said: a tunnel like the tunnel of the jerboa (yarbu'). The meaning: if they found a place in one of these three aspects, even though they are the worst of places, ﴿they would turn towards it﴾, that is, they would return to it. It is said: walla bi-nafsihi when he turned away, and walla ghayrahu when he turned it away. His saying: ﴿while they rush headlong﴾, that is, they hasten with a haste that nothing turns their faces back. From this one says: jamaha al-faras (the horse bolted), and it is a jamuh horse, which is the one that, when it charges, the bridle does not restrain. The intended meaning of the verse is that, due to the intensity of their distress from the Messenger and from the Muslims, they came to be in this state.

Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned three things: al-malja', al-maghārāt, and al-mudkhal, and the closest view is that each of them be understood differently from the others. So al-malja' includes fortresses; al-maghārāt are caves in the mountains; and al-mudkhal is a tunnel beneath the earth, like wells. The author of al-Kashshaf said: it was read as "madkhalan" from dakhala, and "mudkhalan" from adkhala, and it is a place into which they enter themselves; and Ubayy ibn Ka'b read "mutadakhkhalan"; and he read: "lawa'allu ilayhi" (meaning: they would seek refuge), and Anas read: "yajmizūn". He was asked about it and said: yajmahūn, yajmizūn and yashtaddūn are one (in meaning).

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 9, verse 59:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are satisfied; and if they are not given from them, at once they become resentful.﴾ ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger. Indeed, we are to Allah inclined [in hope]."﴾

Know that the purpose of this is to explain another kind of their ugly deeds and disgraceful conduct, namely their criticism of the Messenger on account of his collecting charity (sadaqat) from the wealthy. They say that he favors with it whomever he wishes from among his relatives and those he loves, and they attribute to him that he does not observe justice. There are several issues concerning this verse:

**The first issue:** Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "While the Prophet ﷺ was distributing wealth, Miqdad ibn Dhi al-Khuwaysira al-Tamimi came to him, and he was Hurqus ibn Zuhayr, the origin of the Kharijites (al-Khawarij, the early seceding sect). He said, 'Be just, O Messenger of Allah!' He ﷺ said, 'Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?!' Then this verse was revealed."
